## Steps to deploy Atlas right now

1. Sign in as **atlas-tooling** (top-right chip shows the current customer)
2. Go to **Deploy** — rail on the left, or the button in the titlebar
3. Click **New deployment** (dark button, top right of the page head)
4. Fill the form:
   - **Deployment name** — anything, e.g. `atlas-square-launch`
   - **Revision** — `Precision tooling, measured · rev 1` (only option)
   - **Canvas** — pick **square** or **landscape**. Take one, not "every canvas" — Adstream accepts a single image per ad
   - **Campaign in the tool** — must be `Always On Brand`. This has to match a campaign that already exists in Adstream's selector; the agent stops rather than creating one
   - **Objective** — `Awareness`
   - **Tool fields** JSON — replace the blanks:
     ```json
     {
       "Ad name": "Precision tooling, measured",
       "Audience": "Broad US",
       "Placement": "Feed",
       "Daily budget": "50",
       "Call to action": "Learn More"
     }
     ```
     Leave any value blank and the agent stops rather than guessing — that's deliberate.
5. Click **Create**. The row now appears in the table.
6. Click **Deploy** on that row. The progress panel appears: *box started → driving the tool → recording saved → url read back*, roughly 90–180s.
7. When it finishes, the row shows `published` with a clickable Adstream URL, plus the recording size.

The two fields that decide success are **Campaign** and **Canvas**. Every failure I hit was one of those two — an invented campaign name, or sending all three canvases into a form with one upload field.

## What was there vs what was missing

The recording half was already working: Playwright records the whole browser session inside the sandbox, the context is closed before the box dies so the video actually flushes, and the file is saved to storage with its own SHA and byte count. Nine recordings exist right now, 1.0–2.3 MB each.

What was missing was **playback**. The deploy row printed `recording 1078 KB` as dead text. Evidence nobody can look at is indistinguishable from no evidence, so that rule was only half-enforced.

## What I added

- Each deployment's recording is signed server-side ([deploy/page.tsx](web/app/deploy/page.tsx)) with the **session token** — policy decides whether the row is visible, and the signature is downstream of that, not a way around it. One-hour expiry: long enough to watch, short enough that a pasted URL stops working.
- The row now shows **Watch recording · 997 KB** as a link, which expands an inline `<video controls>` player. One at a time, no autoplay — it's evidence you chose to inspect.
- If a recording row exists but signing fails, it says *"recording saved, could not be signed for playback"* rather than "no recording" — those are different facts and the worse one shouldn't hide the better one.

## Verified

```
signed url          → http 200, 1020650 bytes, content-type video/webm
magic bytes         → 1a45dfa3  (valid WebM, genuinely playable)
atlas-tooling view  → 0 kahua storage keys, no Watch button
```

So the video plays, and another customer signed into the same screen sees neither the recording nor its storage key.

## On "no recording, no deploy"

That invariant is already enforced by the launcher, and I saw it fire today: the run that saved a recording but couldn't read a URL back came out **`unverified`**, not published. The agent also emits a `recording-missing` blocker finding if no video was written at all. `published` requires both a recording and a URL read off the tool's own page.

One honest note: the player is on the Deploy page rows, not on a dedicated run-detail screen. For a deploy with several runs over time you currently see the *latest* recording, since `deployments.recording_artifact_id` holds one reference. Older recordings are all still in storage with their rows intact — they just need a run-history view to reach. Want that next?

**Watch** expands an inline player with the campaign and timestamp in the header, and a link to the published Adstream URL where one exists.

## Why it's keyed on campaign, not deployment

`deployments.recording_artifact_id` holds a single reference, so a deployment run six times kept only the newest video reachable — the other five were in storage with nothing pointing at them. This panel is built from the **artifacts** instead, so it can't lose them.

That also handles a case I'd otherwise have shipped broken: two of your nine recordings belong to deployments **I deleted earlier today**. Deleting a deployment cascades its `deploy_runs` but not its artifacts, so those videos survive with no deployment to name them. They now show the campaign and `rev 2` correctly, with *"deployment deleted"* said plainly rather than appearing as an unlabelled row.

Timestamps render in your local timezone, since "was this the run I watched fail an hour ago" is unanswerable against a UTC string.

## Isolation verified

```
kahua          → 11 signed urls, 9 Watch buttons
atlas-tooling  → 0 signed urls, 0 Watch buttons, "No session recordings yet"
                 0 occurrences of kahua's storage prefix anywhere in the HTML
```

Atlas is signed into the same screen and sees neither the videos nor the storage keys. That's the existing `artifacts` policy doing the work — the URLs are signed **with the session token**, so policy decides what's visible first and the signature only follows. Nothing here trusts the page to filter.

One thing to know for the demo: signed URLs expire after an hour, so a page left open overnight needs a refresh before playback works. The row will say *"could not sign"* rather than showing a dead player.

--- ASSISTANT [2026-08-11 10:08:21] ---
Found it, and it's not the campaign name.

**Adstream has no server.** `app.js` makes **zero** `fetch` calls and stores everything in `localStorage` under one key:

```js
localStorage.setItem(K_ADS, JSON.stringify(SEED_ADS))   // first visit seeds it
localStorage.setItem(K_ADS, JSON.stringify(ads))        // publishing appends here
localStorage.setItem(K_AUTH, '1')                       // even sign-in is local
```

So the sequence was:

1. The sandbox browser opened Adstream, got its **own fresh `localStorage`**, seeded with the same 6 ads you see
2. The agent signed in, filled the form, uploaded the square creative, and published — appending ad **7** to *that browser's* `localStorage`
3. The box was destroyed at the end of the run, and `localStorage` went with it
4. Your browser has its own separate `localStorage`, still holding just the 6 seeded ads

Nothing crossed between them, and nothing could. Two browsers, two independent copies of the same mock. A campaign-name collision would have shown up as `CAMPAIGN_NOT_FOUND` and stopped the run — which is exactly what happened when I passed a name that *didn't* exist. `Always On Brand` matched, which is why it got all the way through.

## One correction to something I told you

I said the `published` status is backed by "a url read back off the tool's own page." That's true, but weaker than it sounded here: this app serves the same 305-byte shell for **every** path, so `ads/7?published=1` returns HTTP 200 whether or not that ad exists. I just checked. Against a real ad tool with a server the read-back means what we want; against this mock it only proves the agent's own session showed it a published page.

**The recording is the real evidence**, and that's not a consolation prize — it's the reason "no recording, no deploy" is the rule. Watch the Kahua session on the Deploy screen and you'll see the ad being created, the creative uploading, and it appearing in that browser's Ads Manager list as row 7.

Two things worth deciding, both quick:

- **Should the deploy assert the ad is in the list before claiming published?** The agent could navigate back to `/ads` and confirm its ad name appears, which is real verification even for a localStorage app. Currently it trusts the post-publish page.
- **Do you want persistence across runs?** If Adstream is meant to accumulate ads, the box would need to carry a `localStorage` seed in, or Adstream needs a server. Worth asking Bhairav which he intended, since it changes what "published" can mean.

--- ASSISTANT [2026-08-11 10:36:03] ---
No — that frame **is** the last step. Here's the publish handler:

```js
const nextId = ads.reduce((m, a) => Math.max(m, a.id), 0) + 1;
const ad = { id: nextId, name, campaign, objective, audience, placements,
             daily_budget, primary_text, cta, width, height, filesize_kb,
             created: nowStamp(), impressions: 0, image: dataUrl };
ads.push(ad);
saveAds(ads);                              // ← written to the list HERE
clearDraft();
navigate('/ads/' + nextId + '?published=1');   // ← then the page you screenshotted
```

The ad is appended to the list **before** that detail page renders. So by the time you see "Ad published" and `Active`, it's already in Ads Manager. There is nothing after `navigate` — that's the end of the flow. The deploy completed properly and nothing was skipped.

**Your timestamp observation is the confirmation, not a problem.** The six seed ads carry hardcoded literal strings — `created: '2025-07-12 09:45:00'` and similar — baked into `SEED_ADS`. A real published ad gets `created: nowStamp()`, so today's date. Different timestamps is exactly what a genuine publish looks like against fixed fixture data.

Two other details that line up: `nextId` is `max(id) + 1`, which with 6 seed ads is **7** — matching `ads/7` precisely. And `impressions: 0`, which is why a new ad wouldn't show the 145.6K-style numbers the seeds have.

**One real thing I found while reading this**, worth knowing before you publish multiple canvases in one session:

```js
try { saveAds(ads); }
catch (err) {
  /* localStorage quota: keep the ad but drop the (large) image blob. */
  ad.image = null;
  saveAds(ads);
}
```

Images are stored as base64 data URLs — a 1080×1080 PNG is roughly 1.4 MB encoded, against a typical 5 MB `localStorage` budget. One ad is fine. Publishing all three canvases in a single box could silently hit the quota and **keep the ad while dropping its image**. That's a case where the verify-in-list check I proposed earns its keep: it would catch an ad that landed without its creative, which is precisely the failure that looks like success.

So: nothing is broken, and the recording shows a complete publish. The remaining work is unchanged — verify-in-list (now with a concrete reason), and narrowing the deploy hydration.

The sandbox's browser wrote ad 7 into **its own** `localStorage` inside the E2B box. Your browser has never had access to that store and never will, no matter how often you refresh. Two isolated copies of the same mock.

So refreshing, re-running, or fixing our code cannot make that ad appear in your browser. The gap is in the target tool, not in the deploy.

## What can actually be done

**Make deploys cumulative and inspectable** — the useful fix. After publishing, the agent reads `localStorage.getItem('<env-secret-redacted>_ads')` and saves it as an artifact alongside the recording. Then the next deploy seeds the box's `localStorage` from that artifact before navigating. Ads accumulate across runs instead of each box starting from the seed six, and you get a machine-readable record of exactly what the tool held at the end of each deploy.

**And it gives you visibility**: with that artifact you can paste one line into your own console to load the same state, so your Ads Manager shows ad 7 with the Kahua creative. Not elegant, but it's the only thing that can bridge two `localStorage` stores.

**Verify-in-list** still belongs on top of that, since it catches the quota case where the ad saves without its image.

## Worth asking Bhairav

Whether Adstream is *intended* to be client-only. If it is, then "published" can only ever mean "the agent completed the flow and recorded it" — which is exactly why the recording requirement exists, and why it's the right primitive. If he meant it to persist server-side, that's a bug in the mock rather than in what we built, and worth knowing before you present.

Want me to build the localStorage export/import? It's contained — agent change plus one artifact role — and it turns this from "trust the video" into "here is the tool's own state, and here's how to load it."

--- ASSISTANT [2026-08-11 10:54:50] ---
Here's the decisive piece of evidence, and it's already in our data.

**Two consecutive deploys both produced `ads/7`.** `pipeline-single-canvas` → `ads/7?published=1`, and then `confirmed-in-list-test` → `ads/7?published=1`. The id comes from `Math.max(...ids) + 1`. If any state were shared or persisted anywhere, the second run would have computed **8**. Both computed 7 because each box started from a fresh browser holding only the 6 seed ads.

And your side confirms it symmetrically: you now have 8 ads. If the sandbox could see your list, its next ad would be **9**. It won't be — it'll be 7 again.

## The reasons, ranked

**1. `localStorage` is scoped to a browser profile, not to an account.** This is the whole explanation. Adstream stores everything in `localStorage['<env-secret-redacted>_ads']`, and `app.js` makes **zero** network calls — no `fetch`, no XHR, no WebSocket. There is no server, so there is nothing for two browsers to share. The sandbox's Chromium on an E2B machine and your Chrome on your laptop each have their own copy, and the box's copy was deleted with the box.

Your 2 manual ads are the same phenomenon from the other direction: they exist only for you, and the sandbox has never seen them.

**2. Not the credentials.** Same account, and signing in only sets `<env-secret-redacted>_auth = '1'` — a boolean. It doesn't scope, fetch, or namespace any data. Every browser that signs in sees its *own* ads.

**3. Not the campaign name.** A name that doesn't exist produces `CAMPAIGN_NOT_FOUND` and stops the run — which I hit when I passed a made-up one. `Always On Brand` matched.

**4. Not a save-before-destroy race.** `ads.push(ad); saveAds(ads);` runs *before* `navigate('/ads/7?published=1')`. The write completes before the confirmation page renders, and the agent has now also reloaded the list and found the row.

**5. Not version skew.** Live bundle is byte-identical to what I analysed — `101ad051…`, 25,035 bytes.

## The test that settles it in 10 seconds

In your browser's console:

```js
JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('<env-secret-redacted>_ads')).map(a => [a.id, a.name])
```

You'll see your 8 — the 6 seeds plus your 2, with no ad from our runs. That's your browser's complete copy of Adstream's universe.

## What would actually make it visible

Only two options, and neither is a bug fix on our side:

- **Export/import the store.** After publishing, the agent saves `localStorage['<env-secret-redacted>_ads']` as an artifact. You get a one-line paste to load that state locally, and the next deploy can seed from it so ads accumulate across runs.
- **Adstream gains a server.** Bhairav's call. If he intended it to persist, this is a gap in the mock, not in the pipeline — and worth confirming before your demo, since it changes what "published" can mean for anyone but the agent.

I'm confident in this, but do your research — if you find a server-side component or shared storage I've missed, that changes the answer and I'd want to know.

No checkboxes — `ROADMAP.md` is an architecture document, not a tracker. But it has a section that bears directly on the gap I just reported to you, so let me read it before I mislead you:
    → Bash: Read the leaderboard decision and remaining sections
    RESULT: ### The leaderboard is a hard finding
    
    728x90 cannot be produced by gpt-image-2 by any route. Outpainting does not
    help, because the 3:1 ceiling constrains the *requested output size*, so no
    edit call can return an 8:1 image either. Filling a 728x90 canvas from a
    generated plate would require cropping or stretching, both forbidden by
    SKILL.md invariant 2.
    
    No other model rescues it either. gpt-image-2's 3:1 is the *most* permissive
    ceiling among current models — Nano Banana Pro caps at 21:9 (2.33:1), Flux is
    practically the same, and Ideogram and Recraft expose preset ratios only. No
    vendor has announced native 8:1 support, because extreme ratios break
    composition. Changing model makes this worse, not better.
    
    ### Settled: skip it
    
    Asked, and answered. **728x90 is a deliberately planted bug** — his words, "this is
    bug #1 we've planted in the process. You can skip that size." He produces it

    ---
    
    ### Stage 7 — The engine
    
    Concurrency to the cap, resume, retry, partial saves, soft delete, re-run.
    
    **Stack** Postgres `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` · E2B lifecycle API · `pg_cron`.
    **Why** The runs table is already the queue, so the cap is a `count(*)`. Asking

    was alive some seconds ago. `pg_cron` removes soft-deleted objects, since Storage
    has no lifecycle rules.

    hydrates to the right tenant, task and revision — identical either way — and the
    hours saved go to deploy.

## What it does

Straight from `packet/starter/README.md`:

| Step | Action | Concurrency |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Emplifi opens a new task | ↕ **both boxes at once** |
| 2 | Kahua opens a new task | ↕ |
| 3 | Kahua edits theirs (pinned comment) | ↕ **both boxes at once** |
| 4 | Emplifi edits theirs (pinned comment) | ↕ |
| 5 | Emplifi opens a second task | alone |

Requests are created through the product's own HTTP API as two separately signed-in customers, and **kit ids are read from the database** rather than written into the script — so the harness doesn't encode which kit belongs to whom, which is the thing the requirement is testing.

--- ASSISTANT [2026-08-11 11:26:21] ---
The harness failed, and every failure is a bug in my script — **nothing about the product was tested and nothing was proven.** No sandboxes ran; the hydration and outputs directories are empty.

## Three bugs, all mine

**1. Wrong field name.** The API takes `headline` as a top-level field:

```js
const headline = (body.headline ?? '').trim()
```

I nested it inside `copy: { headline: ... }`, so every create returned `400 — a campaign name and a headline are required`.

**2. My `log()` writes to stdout, poisoning command substitution.** `create_request` returns its ids via stdout, but `log()` also `tee`s to stdout — so `read -r EMP_RQ EMP_REV` captured a timestamp. Hence `request=11:25:35`. `log()` needs to write to stderr.

**3. `wait` can't see the pids.** `launch()` backgrounds a subshell and echoes `$!`, but capturing that through `$(...)` puts the child in a different shell, so `wait: pid 16293 is not a child of this shell`. The launches need to be backgrounded in the main shell with the pid captured directly, not via a function's stdout.

The cascade: bad ids → launcher had nothing valid to run → all five exited 1 → the collector queried Supabase with an empty request id → `HTTP 400`.

## What was wrong this round

Not a plumbing bug — a **misuse of the launcher that the launcher correctly refused**:

```
hydration is incomplete:
  an edit whose parent revision has an empty tree
  an edit with no instruction to act on
```

I passed `--mode revise` for all five steps. But `revise` means "act on an existing revision", which needs two things a brand-new request doesn't have: a parent with rendered artifacts, and an instruction to act on. `hydrationGaps` caught both and refused to start a box — which is the guard doing its job, and it's the same class of protection that stopped a stale template earlier today.

Two corrections:

- **Steps 1, 2, 5** (new tasks) → `rerender`. **Steps 3, 4** (edits) → `revise`.
- **Edits now target the revision that actually rendered.** I was pointing them at rev 1, which is the empty draft the request is created with. The harness now re-reads the newest revision for each request after the first pair completes, via a `latest_revision` helper.

That second one is a real property of the interleave, not just a script detail: an edit has to attach to whatever the tenant's latest work is, and the harness can't assume a revision number.

I also deleted the three failed `Interleave A/B/C` requests so your sidebars are clean.

## Issue 1 — root cause found, and it's a real product bug

Not a harness problem. In [launch-run.ts](eval/scripts/launch-run.ts#L151), when `--revision` is passed the job is built with `kind` hardcoded:

```ts
job = {
  brandKitId: r.kit_id,
  campaignName: r.campaign_name,
  kind: 'edit',          // ← unconditional, ignores --mode
  ...
}
```

So any launch that continues a revision is an *edit*, whatever `--mode` says. `hydrationGaps` then correctly refuses it, because a first render has no parent tree and no instruction.

**This affects the product, not just my script.** A request created through intake whose first render never happened — exactly the state your failed Northwind request was in — cannot be started by "Re-render", because the launcher will call it an edit and the guard will refuse. It works today only because every request you've re-rendered already had artifacts.

The fix is to derive `kind` from the parent's actual state rather than asserting it: `'edit'` when the parent revision has a tree *and* there are open comments, `'new'` otherwise.

I'm stopping here rather than making that change. It's a real fix to the launcher's core path, and with no context left to test it I'd be shipping an untested edit to the thing that starts every render — which is the opposite of what you asked when you said to ensure rendering isn't affected.

## Where the interleave requirement stands

**Proven:** two tenants, two concurrent sandboxes, each editing their own brand from a pinned comment, both completing — 2 renders each, separate hydration files, no cross-tenant access. That is the substance of what `packet/starter/README.md` asks for.

**Not yet proven:** the full five-step sequence in one pass, blocked by the `kind: 'edit'` bug above.

Evidence on disk at `results/interleave-20260811-113217/` — 2 hydration files, 4 PNGs, per-run logs, `summary.json`. Product code unchanged: `334 passed | 1 skipped`, templates `FRESH`.

```
bk-emplifi-2026  rev1  running   0 render(s)   ← Interleave C
```

1. The launcher creates the run row and flips the revision to `running`
2. **Then** validates hydration — `hydrationGaps` throws
3. The revision is left `running` forever, with no artifacts and no live box
4. Every later launch now sees `status === 'running'`, so `isEmptyDraft` is false → it builds a **successor** revision whose parent is the empty rev 1 → `task: 'edit'` → the same gap error, permanently

That's why the failure was sticky and why steps 3–4 succeeded: they legitimately built rev 2 on a parent, so the edit shape was correct.

**The fix is to validate before mutating** — run `hydrationGaps`/`hydrationLeaks` before creating the run row and setting `running`, so a refused launch leaves the revision exactly as it found it. That also fixes the class of problem, not just this instance: right now *any* early launcher failure poisons the revision for all future attempts.

A secondary repair is needed too: a revision marked `running` with no live sandbox should be reclaimable, or a stuck row is unrecoverable through the UI.

# What "move hydration validation before row creation" means

## The current order

`launch-run.ts` does these things in this sequence:

```
1. resolve the request and revision        (~line 320)
2. INSERT the run row                       (~line 400)
3. SET revision status = 'running'          (~line 400)
4. build the hydration                      (~line 455)
5. check hydrationGaps()  ← throws here     (~line 520)
6. check hydrationLeaks()                   (~line 523)
7. start the sandbox                        (~line 560)
```

Steps 2 and 3 **write to the database**. Step 5 is where the validation happens. So when validation fails, the writes have already landed and there's nothing to undo them — the process throws and exits.

That's what left your rows like this:

```
bk-emplifi-2026  rev1  running  0 render(s)
```

A revision that says it's running, with no artifacts, and no sandbox anywhere — because the box was never started. Step 7 never ran.

## Why that one stuck row breaks every retry

This is the part that makes it more than cosmetic. Further up, the launcher decides whether to fill in the existing revision or make a new one:

```ts
const isEmptyDraft = saved.length === 0 && targetStatus[0]?.status === 'draft'
```

`rev1` now has `status = 'running'`, not `'draft'`. So `isEmptyDraft` is **false**, and the launcher takes the other branch: create a *successor* revision whose parent is rev 1. But rev 1 has no artifacts and there are no comments, so the successor is an "edit" with nothing to edit — and `hydrationGaps` refuses it:

```
an edit whose parent revision has an empty tree
an edit with no instruction to act on
```

Which sets `running` on another row and throws again. **The first failure makes the second failure inevitable, and it's a different error than the original cause** — so you end up debugging the symptom instead of the real problem. That's precisely what happened to me across three runs of the harness.

## The change

Move steps 4–6 above steps 2–3:

```
1. resolve the request and revision
2. build the hydration          ← moved up
3. check hydrationGaps()        ← moved up
4. check hydrationLeaks()       ← moved up
5. INSERT the run row
6. SET revision status = 'running'
7. start the sandbox
```

Now a refused launch touches nothing. The revision stays `draft`, `isEmptyDraft` stays true, and fixing the actual cause and pressing the button again works — instead of hitting a second, misleading error.

There's one ordering constraint to respect: `buildGenerationHydration` takes `runId` and `revisionId`. So either the ids get generated client-side before the insert, or the validation is split — check what doesn't need the run id first, insert, then check the rest. The first is cleaner; `gen_random_uuid()` isn't required to happen in Postgres.

## The general principle

**Validate before you mutate.** A check that runs after the write can only report damage, not prevent it. This is the same shape as the bug where a launch failure was silent because `stdio` was discarded — the system knew what was wrong and had already made it someone else's problem.

And the reason I want to do it with room to test rather than now: this is the code path behind every single render, and getting the id ordering wrong would break generation for all brands, not just the interleave.

    /**
     * A display URL for a private object.
     *
     * The bucket is private and an `<img>` cannot send an Authorization header, so a
     * signed URL is the only way to show an artifact. Signed with the session token, so
     * a customer can only produce a URL for something it was already allowed to read —
     * the signature is not a way around the policy, it is downstream of it.
     */
    export async function sign(token: string, storageKey: string, seconds = 1200): Promise<string | null> {
      const { SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY } = env()
      const response = await fetch(`${SUPABASE_URL}/storage/v1/object/sign/work/${storageKey}`, {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: {
          apikey: SUPABASE_ANON_KEY,
          Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
          'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        },
        body: JSON.stringify({ expiresIn: seconds }),
        cache: 'no-store',
      })
      if (!response.ok) return null
      const { signedURL } = (await response.json()) as { signedURL: string }
      return `${SUPABASE_URL}/storage/v1${signedURL}`
    }

      id: string
      relative_path: string

**Ingest already knew.** It recorded `no-fonts` at upload time — and then marked the kit **`ready`** anyway. So the composer offered it, you filled in a campaign, and the failure surfaced at run time instead.

That's precisely what `AdGeneration.md` says not to do:

> *"If your sizing logic can't produce one of them, that's a finding — say so, rather than letting the request fail at run time."*

Same principle, different subsystem. The launcher's refusal is correct — a kit with **zero** fonts can't produce a compliant render, because every word has to be live text in the brand's typeface and there's nothing to substitute *from*. Kahua's `Barlow Condensed → Barlow` works because Kahua ships Barlow; Meridian ships nothing.

Meridian is one of the deliberately-broken kits I built for exactly this kind of test, so the system catching it is right. **Where** it caught it is wrong.

## Three things to fix, in order

**1. `no-fonts` should be a blocker, not a review.** A kit that cannot render is not `ready`. Meridian should be `blocked` like `vantage-partners`, with the reason attached — so you learn at upload, not four form fields later.

**2. Intake should refuse a kit that can't render.** The composer already warns `this kit is not ingested yet` for non-ready kits. It needs the same treatment for ready-but-unrenderable: disable submit, say *"this brand ships no font files — a render would be off-brand"*. That's cheap now that the Brain section is loading findings.

**3. A failed launch leaves an orphan request.** `/api/request` creates the row, then launches. Your Meridian request exists with no run and no revision that can ever complete. Either the launch precheck runs before the insert, or a failed launch marks the request so the sidebar explains itself.

Note that (3) is the same shape as the reordering I proposed and then retracted this morning — I was wrong about it for `launch-run.ts`, where `running` is set correctly after the box starts. But it's genuinely true for `/api/request`: the request row is committed before the launcher is known to succeed.

I'm out of context to implement these safely, and I've twice today made things worse by editing without room to verify. Worth knowing before you test further: **Northwind and Atlas both render** — Meridian and Vantage are the two intentionally-broken kits, so this doesn't affect your other brands.

Also, you likely want that orphan Meridian request removed from the sidebar before it confuses a demo.

## What was actually happening

No sandbox was ever invoked. The **run row** claimed one existed, and the Review screen honestly reported what the row said.

`launch-run.ts` inserts the run row with `status = 'starting'` at line ~412, validates hydration at ~520, and only creates the box at ~560. Meridian failed the font check in between — so the row sat at `starting` with `sandbox_id = NULL` permanently, and the progress panel seeds itself from exactly that.

I corrected rather than deleted them, because a request that failed for a nameable reason is more useful than one with no history — and "the launcher refused" is a different fact from "nothing happened."

## The permanent fix, not yet done

The row is created before the thing it describes exists. It should be inserted **after** hydration validation passes, so a refused launch leaves no trace of a run that never began. That needs the run id generated before the insert — `buildGenerationHydration` takes `runId` — which is a small change but it sits in the code path behind every render.

I'm not making it now. I've twice today edited with no context left to verify and once left the intake screen broken; doing it to the launcher would take generation down for every brand. I was wrong to retract this fix this morning. My *reasoning* for retracting was sound — I'd misread the interleave failures — but I discarded a real defect along with the bad evidence instead of going to look for the right evidence. These 6 rows were sitting there the whole time.

## The fix

**The bar was reading the wrong signal.** It treated `status in (starting, running)` as "a sandbox is working", but the launcher writes that row *before* it validates hydration and long before it creates a box. So a refused launch left a row that looked active forever.

It now requires **`sandbox_id`** to be present. That's written at the moment the box actually exists, which makes it the honest signal — a row can claim to be starting, but it cannot claim an id it was never given.

**Same flaw in the sidebar**, which I'd have missed if I'd only fixed the panel: it called a request `running` on status alone. It now reads `never started` for a run with no box.

**And the state is explained rather than just hidden:**

> **This run never started.** A run was recorded but no sandbox was ever created, so nothing is in progress. The usual cause is the launcher refusing before it opened a box — a brand missing fonts, or a sandbox image that needs rebuilding.

USER  [2026-08-11 13:17:51]  turn 174
==============================================================================
does the sandbox contunue if I step away from the page?

--- ASSISTANT [2026-08-11 13:18:12] ---
Yes. Nothing about a run depends on the page being open.

**The launcher is detached.** `startLauncher` spawns it with `detached: true`, waits ~9 seconds to catch a fast structural failure so it can report one to you, then calls `child.unref()` and lets go. After that the process is in its own group — it survives you closing the tab, navigating away, and even restarting the dev server.

**The agent saves its own work.** That's the whole point of the save-out design: the box writes artifacts to Supabase through its own scoped credential as it goes. The backend never reaches into the box to collect anything, so there's no browser-side step that could be missed. Anything already saved survives even if the box dies mid-run.

**Coming back shows the truth.** The Review screen seeds its progress panel from the database rather than from tab state, so returning mid-render shows the run still going. That was a deliberate fix — it used to only show progress if *that tab* had pressed the button.

Two real caveats:

- **Don't let the machine sleep.** The E2B sandbox is remote and keeps running, but the launcher orchestrating it is a local process. If your laptop suspends, that process pauses — the box may hit its own timeout while nothing is driving it. Closing the lid is the one thing to avoid; closing the tab is fine.
- **There's a 20-minute budget** per run (`RUN_BUDGET_SECONDS`). A run that exceeds it is stopped, and whatever was saved before that point is kept rather than discarded.

So: stepping away is safe, and you'll see accurate state when you return. If you come back and see **`never started`** with the explanation panel, that's the launcher having refused before opening a box — not a run that vanished while you were gone.

```

```

So the deployment row now claims `published` when one of three ads shipped and the agent explicitly said otherwise.

That's the worst class of error in this system: it reports success over the agent's own contrary finding, and it's exactly the thing the recording requirement exists to prevent. **The launcher should only ever downgrade the agent's outcome, never upgrade it.** The agent knows how many ads it confirmed; the launcher only knows a file exists.

That's a small, high-value fix and it should be first next session.

- **`localStorage` quota** — Adstream stores creatives as base64 against ~5 MB. Square (~1.4 MB encoded) plus six seed ads may leave too little for a second, and its own code silently drops or fails on a full store.
- **A validation rule** on dimensions or file size for non-square creatives.

Distinguishing them needs a look at the recording for `all-canvases-test`, where the disabled button is on camera.

--- ASSISTANT [2026-08-11 13:42:14] ---
# No — nothing to do with approval

Approval is a *precondition*: only an approved revision can be deployed at all, and Kahua rev 2 passed that gate before the run started. `unverified` is about what the agent observed inside the tool.

## What `unverified` means here

It's one of three deployment outcomes, and it exists precisely so "it worked" and "we don't know" can't look the same:

| Outcome | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `published` | every ad confirmed present in the tool's own list, with a recording |
| `unverified` | something completed, but not everything could be confirmed |
| `stopped` | the agent refused to continue |

This run got `unverified` because **1 of 3 ads made it**:

- **square** — uploaded, published, found in Ads Manager ✓
- **landscape** — the tool's `Publish` button stayed disabled after the upload, so it never published
- **portrait** — never attempted; the agent stopped rather than continue past a blocker

The gate I added this session is what produced it: `published` now requires `listConfirmed.size === hydration.publish.length` — three confirmations for three canvases. One confirmation out of three is a partial deploy, and a partial deploy reported as `published` is how a missing ad goes unnoticed for a week.

## So the sequence was

1. The agent confirmed square, hit a hard block on landscape, and stopped
2. It reported `unverified` with a `publish-partial` finding naming square as the one that made it
3. **Then the launcher overwrote it back to `published`** — because it decides on a coarse rule (a recording exists + a URL exists) and applies that after the agent's verdict

So the row you're looking at says `published`, but the truthful answer is the agent's: `unverified`, one ad live. That override is the bug I flagged, and it's the thing to fix first — a launcher that can upgrade the agent's own conclusion makes every `published` status unreliable.

The real blocker underneath all this is landscape not publishing. That's a tool-side refusal — most likely Adstream's `localStorage` quota, since it stores creatives as base64 against roughly 5 MB and square alone is ~1.4 MB encoded. The disabled button is on camera in the `all-canvases-test` recording, which is where I'd look to tell quota from validation.

Both failures are the same class of problem, and neither is the pipeline breaking — it's the agent refusing to guess about a control's state. But they point at a real brittleness.

## What the successful flow proves the controls are

From the square ad that worked:

```
select select[name="campaign"] = Always On Brand
click  input[name="objective"][value="Awareness"]     ← a RADIO, not a select
click  button[type="submit"]
select select[name="audience"] = Broad US
click  input[name="placements"][value="Feed"]          ← a CHECKBOX
fill   input[name="daily_budget"] = 50
```

So objective is a **radio group** and placements are **checkboxes**. Your latest run stopped because it couldn't select the objective "reliably" — most likely it tried `select` on something that needs `click`, or its selector matched more than one element. The correct action is on record in that log line.

## The landscape blocker

Not quota — landscape (833 KB) is smaller than square (1.2 MB), and Adstream's limit is 10 MB. The `Publish` button ships `disabled` in the markup and is enabled by the form's own listeners:

```html
<button id="pub-btn" name="action" value="publish" disabled>Publish</button>
```

The only difference between the two ads was field order:

```
square    → ad_name · cta · primary_text · publish ✓
landscape → ad_name · primary_text · cta · (still disabled)
```

Which means the enablement check runs on field events and didn't re-run after the last action. Selecting a `<select>` that already holds the target value fires no `change`, so the button never re-evaluated. Square got lucky: its last action was a text `fill`, which always fires `input`.

## The fix — one change covering both

The agent needs to **re-read the page after filling the last field and, if the submit control is still disabled, treat that as "validation hasn't re-run" rather than "the tool refused."** Concretely, in the skill: fill fields in the order the form presents them, then re-read; if the primary control is disabled, touch a text field to trigger validation before concluding anything. And prefer `click` for radios and checkboxes, which the successful trace already demonstrates.

That's a skill-and-prompt change plus a template rebuild — no new tools needed.

I'm not making it now. I'm out of context, and a half-changed deploy agent plus a rebuild is how I'd leave you worse off than the current state, which at least fails honestly and loudly.

**Working:** the one-ad-per-canvas loop genuinely works — it created and confirmed square, then correctly started a second flow for landscape.

**Broken, in priority order:**
1. **The launcher overrides the agent's outcome** — it wrote `published` when the agent said `unverified` with 1 of 3 confirmed. A launcher that can upgrade the agent's own verdict makes every `published` unreliable. Fix first.
2. **Form-control brittleness** — the two stops above.

--- ASSISTANT [2026-08-11 13:54:18] ---
Short answer: a minute heartbeat is worth having, but **not for recovery** — and if we add it for recovery we'll have built the wrong thing.

## Why a timer doesn't save work

Progress that's written on a schedule is a *report about* work. What survives a kill is work that was **durable the moment it existed**. That's already the design: `save_work` writes bytes first, then the row, per artifact. A plate generated at minute 3 is durable at minute 3 — a heartbeat at minute 4 adds nothing to its survival.

And the evidence it works is in the logs from today: `2 saved, 0 failed, 27 already recorded`. Save-out is **idempotent** — a retry re-uploading an existing artifact gets a 409 and falls through to the row rather than failing. So artifacts already written are genuinely recovered.

## Where the real hole is, and it's the expensive one

The requirement names it exactly: *"The image model call already succeeded and you've been billed for it."*

A retry today re-runs the agent with the same hydration, and **nothing in that hydration tells it which plates already exist**. So it regenerates them and you pay twice. The bytes from attempt one are sitting in storage, recoverable, and unused.

That's the fix worth making: hydration should carry `already_saved` — the artifacts present for this revision, with digests — and the skill should say *use what exists, generate only what's missing*. That turns a retry from "re-bill and redo" into "resume." One field and one paragraph, and it's the difference between the answer being "a human with database access" and "hit retry."

## What a heartbeat *is* good for

Liveness — telling "still working" from "died at minute nine." Today a killed box leaves the run row saying `running` forever, and the UI can't tell. I fixed the *phantom* case (no `sandbox_id`) but not this one: a box that started and then died still looks alive.

So yes, add it — but as `runs.last_heartbeat_at`, and let the UI treat a run with no heartbeat for ~90 seconds as dead rather than in progress. That's honest reporting, not recovery.

## And the part I'd do first

*"You'll debug all of this faster if runs save their own agent transcripts alongside the work."*

Not built, and they're right. Every tool call, every model decision, saved as an artifact next to the renders. Today that history dies with the box — the `.launch-logs` file only has the launcher's stdout, not the agent's reasoning. That's why I've been reading step traces all day instead of transcripts.

## My answer to "which states does a retry recover"

I can tell you what I believe, but the requirement says *crash it on purpose to find out* — and I haven't. So:

| State | Believed | Verified |
|---|---|---|
| Artifacts saved before the kill | recovered — save-out is idempotent | ✗ |
| Plates already generated | **re-generated and re-billed** | ✗ |
| The revision row | left `running`, needs a human or a PATCH | partly — I fixed the no-sandbox case only |
| Agent transcript | lost entirely | ✓ (not saved at all) |

Proposed order: **transcripts first** (makes everything else debuggable), then **`already_saved` in hydration** (stops the double-billing), then **kill a box on purpose** to replace that table's guesses with facts, then the heartbeat.

Want me to start with transcripts? It's contained — one artifact role, written by the agent it already belongs to.

so if it crashes, retry the sandbox with an updated hydration file basically with the transcipt right

--- ASSISTANT [2026-08-11 13:55:25] ---
Right in the important part — **the retry needs an updated hydration reflecting what already exists.** I'd separate the transcript from that, though, because they serve different readers.

## Two different things

**`already_saved` → into the hydration.** The mechanical facts: which artifacts exist for this revision, their roles, canvases and digests. That's what stops the retry regenerating a plate you've already paid for. Short, structured, and the agent acts on it.

**The transcript → saved as an artifact, for you.** Every tool call and decision, written alongside the renders. This is evidence for a human debugging afterwards — and it's what the requirement asks for (*"I don't need those, but you will"*).

## Why I wouldn't feed the transcript back in

Three reasons, and the first one is the one that bit me today:

1. **Size.** A transcript is tens of thousands of tokens. I blew 339,445 tokens in one turn earlier in this project by letting image data reach the text channel — the same shape of mistake.
2. **It carries the dead ends.** Attempt one's wrong turns become context the retry has to reason past. The *outcome* is useful; the narrative isn't.
3. **It's the wrong abstraction.** "Here's a story about what happened" invites interpretation. "These four files exist, with these digests" is a fact.

## One thing the retry *does* need beyond artifacts

The **decisions**, not the reasoning. If attempt one generated a plate and picked a style — palette keys, logo corner, type scale — the retry has to render against *that*, or you get a set where square and landscape don't match. So:

```
already_saved:     [{ role, canvas, digest, bytes }]        ← don't redo these
prior_decisions:   { the enforced style object }            ← stay consistent with them
transcript:        saved as an artifact, never hydrated     ← for you
```

`prior_decisions` is small because the style is already a strict schema — I made it one after the model invented its own fields.

## So the retry flow becomes

1. Launcher reads what exists for the revision
2. Puts `already_saved` + `prior_decisions` in the hydration
3. Skill says: use what exists, generate only what's missing, stay consistent with prior decisions
4. Agent writes its transcript out with the work, whatever happens

That turns your table from "needs a human with database access" to "hit retry" for the expensive case.

Order I'd build it: transcripts first (makes the rest debuggable), then `already_saved`, then crash a box on purpose to replace my guesses with facts, then the heartbeat for liveness.

I'm out of context to start it now — that's four files plus a template rebuild, and I've twice today left something broken by pushing past this point. First thing next session, and it's the last real gap against `starter/README.md`.

--- ASSISTANT [2026-08-11 13:57:22] ---
Four distinct bugs in those two runs. Ranked by how much they mislead you.

## 1. The launcher reports a recording that belongs to a different run

Both runs end with the **same** recording path:

```
run A saved:  deploy/page@cbeca34667f38cef01c12640206ae6a5.webm  (3810736B)
run A footer: recording: deploy/page@46391fba6c3f7ccaaff628e046a42af8.webm   ← neither

run B saved:  deploy/page@472b71d0b0ca58341124e195ca34be38.webm  (1677896B)
run B footer: recording: deploy/page@46391fba6c3f7ccaaff628e046a42af8.webm   ← same wrong one
```

`page@46391fba…` is from an *earlier* run. The launcher is selecting a recording artifact for the **revision**, not for **this run** — and every deploy of Kahua rev 3 shares that prefix, so it picks a stale one. That means `deployments.recording_artifact_id` may point at the wrong video, and the recordings panel would play the wrong session while claiming it's this deploy's evidence. For a system whose whole verification story is "watch the recording," this is the worst of the four.

Fix: select the recording by `run_id`, not `revision_id`.

## 2. The launcher still overrides the agent's verdict

Run A: agent said **`unverified`** (1 of 3 confirmed). Footer says **`── deploy published`**. Run B got it right only because the agent said `stopped`.

Still the coarse rule — recording exists + URL exists — applied after the agent's outcome. Note run A's URL is `ads/7?published=1`, which is from a *previous* run too. So it upgraded to `published` on the strength of a stale URL and someone else's recording.

## 3. `COPY_MAPPING_MISSING` — a real gap in the hydration

> *Adstream requires one Primary text value, but supplied copy has multiple components (eyebrow, headline, subhead…)*

Adstream has **one** `primary_text` field. We send `copy` as separate components with no statement of which becomes it. Run A guessed `"testing the rendering"`; run B refused. **Same input, different behaviour** — which means it's underspecified, and the agent refusing is the more correct of the two.

Fix: hydration should carry an explicit mapping — `target.field_sources: { "Primary text": "subhead" }` — or the deploy form should collect Primary text directly, like it now collects Ad name. I'd do the latter: it's a tool field, and the person filling the form knows what they want to say.

## 4. The second ad's flow doesn't re-enter the wizard

This is why Publish stays disabled, and it isn't the quota — Adstream *catches* quota errors and drops the image rather than disabling the button.

Look at run A's second ad:

```
click a[href="/ads/new/step1"]     ← first ad: enters the wizard properly
...
goto url = https://…/ads           ← second ad: goes to the LIST
select select[name="campaign"]     ← then interacts with wizard controls anyway
```

It never re-entered `/ads/new/step1`. So it was driving a form instance whose listeners were never wired for that pass — and `pub-btn` ships `disabled` in the markup, enabled only by those listeners. Hence "remained disabled after upload" on the second ad in **both** runs, regardless of file size.

Fix in the skill: after publishing, navigate to the *create* URL to start the next ad, not the list — and re-read the page to confirm you're on step 1 before filling anything.

## Also worth noting: the `read_page` fix is working

Run B used `#campaign`, `#next-btn`, `input[value='Traffic']` — ids and values that weren't visible to the agent before this morning's change. That's why it got further into the form and failed on a *semantic* problem (copy mapping) rather than a *perception* one.

## Order I'd fix them

1. **Recording selected by `run_id`** — evidence pointing at the wrong run poisons everything else
2. **Launcher must never upgrade the agent's outcome** — only downgrade
3. **Primary text as an explicit form field** — removes the guess entirely
4. **Skill: re-enter the create flow per ad** — unblocks ads 2 and 3

1 and 2 are in `launch-deploy.ts` and are small. 3 is a form field plus a hydration key. 4 is skill text plus a template rebuild.

I'm out of context to implement these safely — but all four are precisely located, and none touch generation.

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)

## The Four Phases

You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.

### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation

**BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**

1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
   - Don't skip past errors or warnings
   - They often contain the exact solution
   - Read stack traces completely
   - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes

2. **Reproduce Consistently**
   - Can you trigger it reliably?
   - What are the exact steps?
   - Does it happen every time?
   - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess

3. **Check Recent Changes**
   - What changed that could cause this?
   - Git diff, recent commits
   - New dependencies, config changes
   - Environmental differences

4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**

   **WHEN system has multiple components (CI → build → signing, API → service → database):**

   **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
   ```
   For EACH component boundary:
     - Log what data enters component
     - Log what data exits component
     - Verify environment/config propagation
     - Check state at each layer

   Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
   THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
   THEN investigate that specific component
   ```

   **Example (multi-layer system):**
   ```bash
   # Layer 1: Workflow
   echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
   echo "IDENTITY: ${IDENTITY:+SET}${IDENTITY:-UNSET}"

   # Layer 2: Build script
   echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
   env | grep IDENTITY || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"

   # Layer 3: Signing script
   echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
   security list-keychains
   security find-identity -v

   # Layer 4: Actual signing
   codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
   ```

   **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets → workflow ✓, workflow → build ✗)

5. **Trace Data Flow**

   **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**

   See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.

   **Quick version:**
   - Where does bad value originate?
   - What called this with bad value?
   - Keep tracing up until you find the source
   - Fix at source, not at symptom

### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis

**Find the pattern before fixing:**

1. **Find Working Examples**
   - Locate similar working code in same codebase
   - What works that's similar to what's broken?

2. **Compare Against References**
   - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
   - Don't skim - read every line
   - Understand the pattern fully before applying

3. **Identify Differences**
   - What's different between working and broken?
   - List every difference, however small
   - Don't assume "that can't matter"

4. **Understand Dependencies**
   - What other components does this need?
   - What settings, config, environment?
   - What assumptions does it make?

### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing

**Scientific method:**

1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
   - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
   - Write it down
   - Be specific, not vague

2. **Test Minimally**
   - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
   - One variable at a time
   - Don't fix multiple things at once

3. **Verify Before Continuing**
   - Did it work? Yes → Phase 4
   - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
   - DON'T add more fixes on top

4. **When You Don't Know**
   - Say "I don't understand X"
   - Don't pretend to know
   - Ask for help
   - Research more

### Phase 4: Implementation

**Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**

1. **Create Failing Test Case**
   - Simplest possible reproduction
   - Automated test if possible
   - One-off test script if no framework
   - MUST have before fixing
   - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests

2. **Implement Single Fix**
   - Address the root cause identified
   - ONE change at a time
   - No "while I'm here" improvements
   - No bundled refactoring

3. **Verify Fix**
   - Test passes now?
   - No other tests broken?
   - Issue actually resolved?
   - Use the `superpowers:verification-before-completion` skill before claiming success

4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**
   - STOP
   - Count: How many fixes have you tried?
   - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information
   - **If ≥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**
   - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion

5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**

   **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**
   - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place
   - Fixes require "massive refactoring" to implement
   - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere

   **STOP and question fundamentals:**
   - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?
   - Are we "sticking with it through sheer inertia"?
   - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?

   **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**

   This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.

## Red Flags - STOP and Follow Process

If you catch yourself thinking:
- "Quick fix for now, investigate later"
- "Just try changing X and see if it works"
- "Add multiple changes, run tests"
- "Skip the test, I'll manually verify"
- "It's probably X, let me fix that"
- "I don't fully understand but this might work"
- "Pattern says X but I'll adapt it differently"
- "Here are the main problems: [lists fixes without investigation]"
- Proposing solutions before tracing data flow
- **"One more fix attempt" (when already tried 2+)**
- **Each fix reveals new problem in different place**

**ALL of these mean: STOP. Return to Phase 1.**

**If 3+ fixes failed:** Question the architecture (see Phase 4.5)

## your human partner's Signals You're Doing It Wrong

**Watch for these redirections:**
- "Is that not happening?" - You assumed without verifying
- "Will it show us...?" - You should have added evidence gathering
- "Stop guessing" - You're proposing fixes without understanding
- "Ultra-think this" - Question fundamentals, not just symptoms
- "We're stuck?" (frustrated) - Your approach isn't working

**When you see these:** STOP. Return to Phase 1.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Issue is simple, don't need process" | Simple issues have root causes too. Process is fast for simple bugs. |
| "Emergency, no time for process" | Systematic debugging is FASTER than guess-and-check thrashing. |
| "Just try this first, then investigate" | First fix sets the pattern. Do it right from the start. |
| "I'll write test after confirming fix works" | Untested fixes don't stick. Test first proves it. |
| "Multiple fixes at once saves time" | Can't isolate what worked. Causes new bugs. |
| "Reference too long, I'll adapt the pattern" | Partial understanding guarantees bugs. Read it completely. |
| "I see the problem, let me fix it" | Seeing symptoms ≠ understanding root cause. |
| "One more fix attempt" (after 2+ failures) | 3+ failures = architectural problem. Question pattern, don't fix again. |

## Quick Reference

| Phase | Key Activities | Success Criteria |
|-------|---------------|------------------|
| **1. Root Cause** | Read errors, reproduce, check changes, gather evidence | Understand WHAT and WHY |
| **2. Pattern** | Find working examples, compare | Identify differences |
| **3. Hypothesis** | Form theory, test minimally | Confirmed or new hypothesis |
| **4. Implementation** | Create test, fix, verify | Bug resolved, tests pass |

## When Process Reveals "No Root Cause"

If systematic investigation reveals issue is truly environmental, timing-dependent, or external:

1. You've completed the process
2. Document what you investigated
3. Implement appropriate handling (retry, timeout, error message)
4. Add monitoring/logging for future investigation

**But:** 95% of "no root cause" cases are incomplete investigation.

## Supporting Techniques

These techniques are part of systematic debugging and available in this directory:

- **`root-cause-tracing.md`** - Trace bugs backward through call stack to find original trigger
- **`defense-in-depth.md`** - Add validation at multiple layers after finding root cause
- **`condition-based-waiting.md`** - Replace arbitrary timeouts with condition polling

    245	const claims = decodePayload(token)
    246	const b64 = (value: object) => Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(value)).toString('base64url')
    247	const deployToken = (() => {
    248	  const header = b64({ alg: 'HS256', typ: 'JWT' })
    249	  const body = b64({ ...claims, role: 'sandbox_deploy' })
    250	  const signature = createHmac('sha256', env.SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET as string)
    251	    .update(`${header}.${body}`)
    252	    .digest()
    253	    .toString('base64url')
    254	  return `${header}.${body}.${signature}`
    255	})()
    256	
    257	const sandboxEnv: Record<string, string> = {
    258	  SUPABASE_URL,
    259	  SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: env.SUPABASE_ANON_KEY as string,
    260	  CQ_RUN_TOKEN: deployToken,
    261	  CQ_RUN_ID: run.id,
    262	  CQ_REVISION_ID: revision.id,
    263	  CQ_WORK_PREFIX: `${revision.request_id}/rev-${revision.n}`,
    264	  CQ_WORK_DIR: '/home/user/work',
    265	  CQ_RECORDING_DIR: '/home/user/work/deploy',
    266	  CQ_AGENT_MODEL: env.CQ_AGENT_MODEL ?? 'gpt-5.6-sol',
    267	  OPENAI_API_KEY: env.OPENAI_API_KEY as string,
    268	  PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH: '/ms-playwright',
    269	  DEPLOY_USERNAME: env.DEPLOY_USERNAME ?? '',
    270	  DEPLOY_PASSWORD: env.DEPLOY_PASSWORD ?? '',
    271	}
    272	for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(sandboxEnv)) {
    273	  if (value === SERVICE_ROLE) throw new Error(`refusing: ${key} carries service_role`)
    274	  if (value === env.SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET) throw new Error(`refusing: ${key} carries the JWT secret`)
    275	}
    276	
    277	process.env.E2B_API_KEY = env.E2B_API_KEY
    278	const sandbox = await Sandbox.create('cq-deployment', {
    279	  timeoutMs: RUN_BUDGET_SECONDS * 1000,
    280	  envs: sandboxEnv,
    281	})
    282	console.log(`deployment ${deployment.name}\nsandbox ${sandbox.sandboxId}\npublishing ${publish.length} canvas(es)`)
    283	
    284	await rest(`runs?id=eq.${run.id}`, {
    285	  method: 'PATCH',
    286	  body: JSON.stringify({ sandbox_id: sandbox.sandboxId, status: 'running' }),
    287	})
    288	await rest(`deploy_runs?id=eq.${deployRun.id}`, { method: 'PATCH', body: JSON.stringify({ status: 'running' }) })
    289	await sandbox.files.write('/home/user/hydration.json', JSON.stringify(hydration, null, 2))
    290	
    291	let exitReason = 'completed'
    292	try {
    293	  const result = await sandbox.commands.run('cd /home/user && ./node_modules/.bin/tsx agent.deploy.ts 2>&1', {
    294	    timeoutMs: RUN_BUDGET_SECONDS * 1000,
    295	    onStdout: (line: string) => { process.stdout.write(`  ${line}`) },
    296	    onStderr: (line: string) => { process.stderr.write(`  ${line}`) },
    297	  })
    298	  if (result.exitCode !== 0) exitReason = `agent exited ${result.exitCode}`
    299	} catch (error) {
    300	  exitReason = `agent failed: ${(error as Error).message.slice(0, 200)}`
    301	  console.error(`\n${exitReason}`)
    302	} finally {
    303	  const recordings = await rest<{ id: string; relative_path: string }[]>(
    304	    `artifacts?revision_id=eq.${revision.id}&role=eq.recording&select=id,relative_path`,
    305	  )
    306	  const [current] = await rest<{ status: string; verified_url: string | null }[]>(
    307	    `deployments?id=eq.${deployment.id}&select=status,verified_url`,
    308	  )
    309	
    310	  /**
    311	   * A deploy is `published` only with a recording AND a url read back off the page.
    312	   * Anything else is `unverified`, however cheerfully the agent reported.
    313	   */
    314	  const evidenced = recordings.length > 0 && Boolean(current?.verified_url)
    315	  const status = exitReason === 'completed' ? (evidenced ? 'published' : 'unverified') : 'failed'
    316	
    317	  await rest(`deployments?id=eq.${deployment.id}`, {
    318	    method: 'PATCH',
    319	    body: JSON.stringify({
    320	      status,
    321	      recording_artifact_id: recordings[0]?.id ?? null,
    322	      verified_note: evidenced ? 'recording saved and url read back' : 'no recording or no url read back',
    323	    }),
    324	  })
    325	  await rest(`deploy_runs?id=eq.${deployRun.id}`, {
    326	    method: 'PATCH',
    327	    body: JSON.stringify({
    328	      status: exitReason === 'completed' ? 'completed' : 'failed',
    329	      exit_reason: exitReason,
    330	      ended_at: new Date().toISOString(),
    331	    }),
    332	  })
    333	  await rest(`runs?id=eq.${run.id}`, {
    334	    method: 'PATCH',
    335	    body: JSON.stringify({ status: exitReason === 'completed' ? 'completed' : 'failed', exit_reason: exitReason, ended_at: new Date().toISOString() }),
    336	  })
    337	
    338	  await sandbox.kill()
    339	  console.log(`\n── deploy ${status}`)
    340	  console.log(`   recording: ${recordings[0]?.relative_path ?? 'NONE'}`)
    341	  console.log(`   verified url: ${current?.verified_url ?? 'none'}`)
    342	}

    RESULT: 1	/**
    2	 * The deployment agent. Runs inside the deploy box, and is the only thing that does.
    3	 *
    4	 * It drives someone else's interface, which makes it different from the generation
    5	 * agent in one important way: **there is no undo out there.** A half-created campaign
    6	 * has to be found by a person before it can be removed, so the bias throughout is to
    7	 * stop rather than guess.
    8	 *
    9	 * The division of labour again:
    10	 *
    11	 *   deterministic — download the artifacts, verify their bytes, start the recording,
    12	 *                   read back the result, save. All failure-checked in code.
    13	 *   judgement     — reading a page and deciding which control does what. The interface
    14	 *                   is not ours and can change, so a recorded click path is a
    15	 *                   description of one past visit, not a rule about this one.
    16	 *
    17	 * The recording is not a nicety. Playwright flushes video on context close, so a box
    18	 * killed first loses it — and a deploy with no recording cannot be evidenced. Context
    19	 * close therefore happens before the run reports anything.
    20	 */
    21	import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process'
    22	import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
    23	import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
    24	import { join } from 'node:path'
    25	import { Agent, run, tool } from '@openai/agents'
    26	import { chromium, type BrowserContext, type Page } from 'playwright'
    27	import { z } from 'zod'
    28	
    29	const HOME = process.env.HOME ?? '/home/user'
    30	const WORK = process.env.CQ_WORK_DIR ?? join(HOME, 'work')
    31	const RECORDING_DIR = process.env.CQ_RECORDING_DIR ?? join(WORK, 'deploy')
    32	const ARTIFACT_DIR = join(HOME, 'artifacts')
    33	const MODEL = process.env.CQ_AGENT_MODEL ?? 'gpt-5.6-sol'

    35	interface DeployHydration {
    36	  kind: 'deploy'
    37	  run_id: string
    38	  revision_id: string
    39	  brand_kit_id: string
    40	  publish: {
    41	    canvas: string
    42	    relative_path: string
    43	    signed_url: string
    44	    width: number
    45	    height: number
    46	  }[]
    47	  campaign: { name: string; copy: Record<string, string | null> }
    48	  target: {
    49	    tool: string
    50	    entry_url: string
    51	    credential_env: string[]

    53	    campaign: string | null

    55	    notes: string | null
    56	    /** Whatever else the tool's form asks for. Absent values are a reason to stop. */
    57	    fields: Record<string, string>

    59	  skill: { invoke: string; mount: { path: string } }
    60	  resolution_order: string[]
    61	  outputs: { root: string; save_with: string; recording_required: true; expected_tree: string[] }
    62	  limits: { sandbox_timeout_seconds: number }
    63	}
    64	
    65	const hydration: DeployHydration = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(HOME, 'hydration.json'), 'utf8'))
    66	const skillBody = readFileSync(hydration.skill.mount.path, 'utf8')

    68	mkdirSync(ARTIFACT_DIR, { recursive: true })
    69	mkdirSync(RECORDING_DIR, { recursive: true })

    71	const findings: { code: string; severity: string; detail: string }[] = []
    72	const steps: string[] = []
    73	
    74	function note(step: string) {
    75	  steps.push(`${new Date().toISOString().slice(11, 19)} ${step}`)
    76	  console.log(`[deploy] ${step}`)
    77	}
    78	
    79	/**
    80	 * Downloads every artifact and checks its size against the manifest.
    81	 *
    82	 * Done before the browser opens, because an artifact that will not download is a
    83	 * blocker at the cheapest possible moment — before anything has been created in
    84	 * someone else's account.
    85	 */
    86	async function fetchArtifacts() {
    87	  const local: { canvas: string; path: string; bytes: number; digest: string }[] = []
    88	  for (const item of hydration.publish) {
    89	    const response = await fetch(item.signed_url)
    90	    if (!response.ok) {
    91	      throw new Error(`could not download ${item.relative_path}: ${response.status}`)
    92	    }
    93	    const bytes = Buffer.from(await response.arrayBuffer())
    94	    const path = join(ARTIFACT_DIR, `${item.canvas}.png`)
    95	    writeFileSync(path, bytes)
    96	    local.push({
    97	      canvas: item.canvas,
    98	      path,
    99	      bytes: bytes.length,
    100	      digest: createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex'),
    101	    })
    102	    note(`downloaded ${item.canvas} · ${bytes.length}B · ${item.width}x${item.height}`)
    103	  }
    104	  if (local.length === 0) throw new Error('nothing to publish')
    105	  return local
    106	}
    107	
    108	const artifacts = await fetchArtifacts()

    110	/**
    111	 * A recording context, opened before the first navigation.
    112	 *
    113	 * `recordVideo` writes on close, so nothing here is optional and nothing may be
    114	 * reordered: browser, then context with video, then any page at all.
    115	 */
    116	let context: BrowserContext | null = null
    117	let page: Page | null = null
    118	
    119	const browser = await chromium.launch()
    120	context = await browser.newContext({
    121	  viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 },
    122	  recordVideo: { dir: RECORDING_DIR, size: { width: 1440, height: 900 } },
    123	})

    125	note('recording started')

    127	const currentPage = () => page as Page
    128	
    129	/** What is on screen, as text the model can reason about. */
    130	const readTool = tool({
    131	  name: 'read_page',
    132	  description:
    133	    'Return the current URL, the visible text, and every interactive control with its ' +
    134	    'name and label. Call this after every navigation — the interface is not ours and ' +
    135	    'a remembered layout is not a reliable one.',
    136	  parameters: z.object({}),
    137	  async execute() {
    138	    const p = currentPage()
    139	    await p.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded').catch(() => {})
    140	    const controls: string[] = []
    141	    for (const el of await p.locator('input, select, textarea, button, a[href]').all()) {
    142	      const tag = await el.evaluate((n) => n.tagName.toLowerCase()).catch(() => '?')
    143	      const type = await el.getAttribute('type')
    144	      const name = await el.getAttribute('name')
    145	      const href = await el.getAttribute('href')
    146	      const placeholder = await el.getAttribute('placeholder')
    147	      /**
    148	       * `value`, `id`, `checked` and the associated label text.
    149	       *
    150	       * Without these a radio group is invisible. Three
    151	       * `input[type=radio][name="objective"]` elements have no inner text, no
    152	       * placeholder and the same name, so they rendered as three identical lines and
    153	       * the agent stopped rather than guess which one meant "Awareness" — correctly,
    154	       * but for a reason that was ours rather than the tool's.
    155	       *
    156	       * The label is looked up two ways because forms do it both ways: a `<label for>`
    157	       * elsewhere in the document, or a `<label>` wrapping the input.
    158	       */
    159	      const value = await el.getAttribute('value')
    160	      const id = await el.getAttribute('id')
    161	      const checked = await el.evaluate((n) => (n as HTMLInputElement).checked ?? null).catch(() => null)
    162	      const disabled = await el.evaluate((n) => (n as HTMLInputElement).disabled ?? false).catch(() => false)
    163	      const labelled = await el
    164	        .evaluate((n) => {
    165	          const self = n as HTMLInputElement
    166	          if (self.id) {
    167	            const forLabel = document.querySelector(`label[for="${self.id}"]`)
    168	            if (forLabel?.textContent?.trim()) return forLabel.textContent.trim()
    169	          }
    170	          return n.closest('label')?.textContent?.trim() ?? ''
    171	        })
    172	        .catch(() => '')
    173	      const inner = (await el.innerText().catch(() => '')).trim()
    174	      const label = (inner || labelled).slice(0, 48)
    175	
    176	      // Options, so a select is choosable without a second call to discover them.
    177	      const options =
    178	        tag === 'select'
    179	          ? await el
    180	              .evaluate((n) => [...(n as HTMLSelectElement).options].map((o) => o.value))
    181	              .catch(() => [])
    182	          : []
    183	
    184	      controls.push(
    185	        `${tag}${type ? `[${type}]` : ''}` +
    186	          `${name ? ` name="${name}"` : ''}` +
    187	          `${value !== null ? ` value="${value}"` : ''}` +
    188	          `${id ? ` id="${id}"` : ''}` +
    189	          `${placeholder ? ` placeholder="${placeholder}"` : ''}` +
    190	          `${label ? ` text="${label}"` : ''}` +
    191	          `${checked === true ? ' checked' : ''}` +
    192	          `${disabled ? ' DISABLED' : ''}` +
    193	          `${options.length ? ` options=[${options.join('|')}]` : ''}` +
    194	          `${href ? ` href="${href}"` : ''}`,
    195	      )
    196	    }
    197	    return {
    198	      url: p.url(),
    199	      title: await p.title(),
    200	      text: (await p.locator('body').innerText().catch(() => '')).slice(0, 2500),
    201	      controls: controls.slice(0, 60),
    202	    }
    203	  },
    204	})

    206	const actTool = tool({
    207	  name: 'act',
    208	  description:
    209	    'Do one thing on the page: navigate, click, fill a field, or select an option. ' +
    210	    'Returns the page afterwards so you can see what happened.',
    211	  parameters: z.object({
    212	    action: z.enum(['goto', 'click', 'fill', 'select', 'upload', 'press']),
    213	    /** A CSS selector, or visible text for a click. */
    214	    target: z.string(),
    215	    value: z.string().nullable().describe('the text to type, option to select, or url'),
    216	  }),
    217	  async execute({ action, target, value }) {
    218	    const p = currentPage()
    219	    try {
    220	      if (action === 'goto') {
    221	        const url = new URL(value ?? target, hydration.target.entry_url)
    222	        // One host. A deploy box that can be steered to another site is a much larger
    223	        // problem than a failed deploy.
    224	        if (url.host !== new URL(hydration.target.entry_url).host) {
    225	          return { error: `refusing to leave ${new URL(hydration.target.entry_url).host}` }
    226	        }
    227	        await p.goto(url.toString(), { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' })
    228	      } else if (action === 'click') {
    229	        const byText = p.getByRole('button', { name: target, exact: false })
    230	        const byLink = p.getByRole('link', { name: target, exact: false })
    231	        if (await byText.count()) await byText.first().click()
    232	        else if (await byLink.count()) await byLink.first().click()
    233	        else await p.locator(target).first().click()
    234	        await p.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded').catch(() => {})
    235	      } else if (action === 'fill') {
    236	        await p.locator(target).first().fill(value ?? '')
    237	      } else if (action === 'select') {
    238	        await p.locator(target).first().selectOption({ label: value ?? '' }).catch(async () => {
    239	          await p.locator(target).first().selectOption(value ?? '')
    240	        })
    241	      } else if (action === 'upload') {
    242	        const artifact = artifacts.find((a) => a.canvas === (value ?? '')) ?? artifacts[0]
    243	        await p.locator(target).first().setInputFiles(artifact.path)
    244	        note(`uploaded ${artifact.canvas} (${artifact.bytes}B)`)
    245	      } else if (action === 'press') {
    246	        await p.locator(target).first().press(value ?? 'Enter')
    247	      }
    248	      await p.waitForTimeout(400)
    249	      note(`${action} ${target}${value ? ` = ${value.slice(0, 40)}` : ''}`)
    250	      return {
    251	        ok: true,
    252	        url: p.url(),
    253	        text: (await p.locator('body').innerText().catch(() => '')).slice(0, 1200),
    254	      }
    255	    } catch (error) {
    256	      // Returned, not thrown: a wrong selector should let the model look again rather
    257	      // than end the run half way through a form.
    258	      return { error: (error as Error).message.slice(0, 240) }
    259	    }
    260	  },
    261	})
