    308	/**
    309	 * Go back to the list and find the ad. Required before claiming `published`.
    310	 *
    311	 * The confirmation page is the tool telling you it worked. The list is the tool
    312	 * showing you it worked, and those are not the same claim — the publish handler can
    313	 * save an ad and silently drop its image when storage is full, which looks identical
    314	 * on the confirmation screen and wrong in the list.
    315	 *
    316	 * It also fixes an ordering mistake: the recording used to end on the confirmation
    317	 * page, so the video stopped one screen before the only screen that proves anything.
    318	 * Whatever this finds, the row is on camera.
    319	 */
    320	const confirmTool = tool({
    321	  name: 'confirm_in_list',
    322	  description:
    323	    'Return to the ad list and confirm your ad is really there. Call this after publishing ' +
    324	    'and BEFORE record_outcome — an outcome of `published` is only accepted once this has ' +
    325	    'found the ad. Give it a moment first: the confirmation toast clears after a few seconds ' +
    326	    'and the list needs to be reloaded, not remembered.',
    327	  parameters: z.object({
    328	    ad_name: z.string().describe('the exact ad name to look for in the list'),
    329	    list_url: z.string().describe('the url of the list page, e.g. the Ads Manager link'),
    330	  }),
    331	  async execute({ ad_name, list_url }) {
    332	    // Long enough for the toast to clear and any write to settle, so the list is read
    333	    // rather than a stale render of it.
    334	    const active = currentPage()
    335	    await active.waitForTimeout(4000)

    337	    await active.waitForTimeout(1500)

    340	    const found = text.includes(ad_name)

    342	    await active.waitForTimeout(2500)
    343	
    344	    if (found) listConfirmed.add(ad_name)
    345	    note(`list check for "${ad_name}" at ${list_url}: ${found ? 'FOUND' : 'NOT FOUND'}`)
    346	    if (!found) {
    347	      findings.push({
    348	        code: 'ad-absent-from-list',
    349	        severity: 'blocker',
    350	        detail:
    351	          `the tool reported publishing "${ad_name}" but it is not in the list at ${list_url} — ` +
    352	          'the confirmation page cannot be taken as evidence on its own',
    353	      })
    354	    }
    355	    return {
    356	      found,
    357	      // The row as the tool renders it, so the result file carries what was seen.
    358	      list_excerpt: text.slice(0, 1200),
    359	    }
    360	  },

    363	/**
    364	 * Ad names confirmed present in the tool's own list.
    365	 *
    366	 * A set rather than a flag, because one deploy publishes one ad per canvas. Counting
    367	 * them is what makes a partial deploy visible: two of three confirmed is a different
    368	 * fact from three of three, and the earlier single-value version could not tell them
    369	 * apart.
    370	 */
    371	const listConfirmed = new Set<string>()
    372	
    373	const verifyTool = tool({
    374	  name: 'record_outcome',
    375	  description:
    376	    'Report the outcome. Call this exactly once, at the end. `published` requires BOTH a url ' +
    377	    'you actually read off the page after publishing — not one you expected — and a successful ' +
    378	    'confirm_in_list call.',
    379	  parameters: z.object({
    380	    outcome: z.enum(['published', 'unverified', 'stopped']),
    381	    verified_url: z.string().nullable(),
    382	    note: z.string(),
    383	  }),
    384	  async execute({ outcome, verified_url, note: detail }) {
    385	    /**
    386	     * `published` is downgraded when the list never confirmed it.
    387	     *
    388	     * Enforced here rather than trusted to the prompt, because this is the one claim
    389	     * the whole deploy is judged on and a model that skipped a step should not be
    390	     * able to assert it anyway.
    391	     */
    392	    let effective = outcome
    393	    const expected = hydration.publish.length
    394	    if (outcome === 'published' && listConfirmed.size < expected) {
    395	      /**
    396	       * Partial is not published.
    397	       *
    398	       * Every canvas in `publish` is an ad someone is expecting to be live. Reporting
    399	       * `published` with two of three in the tool would leave the third missing and

    443	          }),

    446	      } catch (error) {

    448	      }
    449	    }

    function publishAd(file, name, primaryText, cta, btn) {
      if (!file) return;
      if (file.size > MAX_UPLOAD) { showToast('Image exceeds the 10 MB limit'); return; }
      btn.disabled = true;
    
      const reader = new FileReader();
      reader.onload = function (ev) {
        const dataUrl = ev.target.result;
        const img = new Image();
        img.onload = function () {
          const draft = getDraft();
          const ads = getAds();
          const nextId = ads.reduce(function (m, a) { return Math.max(m, a.id); }, 0) + 1;
          const ad = {
            id: nextId,
            name: name,
            campaign: draft.campaign,
            objective: draft.objective,
            audience: draft.audience,
            placements: draft.placements,
            daily_budget: parseFloat(draft.daily_budget),
            primary_text: primaryText,
            cta: cta,
            width: img.naturalWidth,
            height: img.naturalHeight,
            filesize_kb: file.size / 1024,
            created: nowStamp(),
            impressions: 0,
            image: dataUrl,
          };
          ads.push(ad);
          try {
            saveAds(ads);
          } catch (err) {
            /* localStorage quota: keep the ad but drop the (large) image blob. */
            ad.image = null;
            saveAds(ads);
          }
          clearDraft();
          navigate('/ads/' + nextId + '?published=1');
        };
        img.onerror = function () { showToast('Could not read that image'); btn.disabled = false; };
        img.src = dataUrl;
      };
      reader.onerror = function () { showToast('Could not read that file'); btn.disabled = false; };
      reader.readAsDataURL(file);
    }

    19	 * brand rows — neither of which a person may do.
    20	 */
    21	const ID = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,48}$/
    22	
    23	export async function POST(request: Request) {
    24	  const store = await cookies()
    25	  const token = store.get('cq_session')?.value
    26	  // A session is required even to create a new customer: this is an operator action in
    27	  // a single-tenant local deployment, not a public sign-up.
    28	  if (!token || !verifyUserToken(token)) {
    29	    return Response.json({ error: 'not signed in' }, { status: 401 })
    30	  }
    31	
    32	  const form = await request.formData()
    33	  const customerId = String(form.get('customer_id') ?? '').trim().toLowerCase()
    34	  const kitId = String(form.get('kit_id') ?? '').trim().toLowerCase()
    35	  const displayName = String(form.get('display_name') ?? '').trim() || customerId
    36	
    37	  if (!ID.test(customerId)) {
    38	    return Response.json({ error: 'customer id must be lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens' }, { status: 400 })
    39	  }
    40	  if (!ID.test(kitId)) {
    41	    return Response.json({ error: 'kit id must be lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens' }, { status: 400 })
    42	  }
    43	
    44	  // Refuse to touch anything that exists. An "add customer" that can adopt an existing
    45	  // customer or kit is a way to reach another tenant's data by naming it.
    46	  const existingKit = await serviceFetch(`/rest/v1/brand_kits?id=eq.${encodeURIComponent(kitId)}&select=id`)
    47	  if (Array.isArray(existingKit) && existingKit.length) {
    48	    return Response.json({ error: `kit ${kitId} already exists` }, { status: 409 })
    49	  }
    50	  const existingCustomer = await serviceFetch(
    51	    `/rest/v1/brand_kits?customer_id=eq.${encodeURIComponent(customerId)}&select=id&limit=1`,
    52	  )
    53	  if (Array.isArray(existingCustomer) && existingCustomer.length) {
    54	    return Response.json(
    55	      { error: `customer ${customerId} already exists — upload into its kit instead` },
    56	      { status: 409 },
    57	    )
    58	  }
    59	
    60	  const files = form.getAll('files').filter((f): f is File => f instanceof File)
    61	  if (files.length === 0) return Response.json({ error: 'no files were dropped' }, { status: 400 })
    62	
    63	  /**
    64	   * Files are written to a staging directory, then ingested from there.
    65	   *
    66	   * Ingest already knows how to read a brain off disk, resolve its manifest, index its
    67	   * fonts and record every finding. Reimplementing that against an upload stream would
    68	   * mean two code paths deciding what a brand is, and they would drift.
    69	   */
    70	  const staging = join(process.cwd(), '..', '.staging-kits', kitId)
    71	  rmSync(staging, { recursive: true, force: true })
    72	  mkdirSync(staging, { recursive: true })
    73	
    74	  const stored: string[] = []
    75	  for (const file of files) {
    76	    // `webkitRelativePath` arrives when a whole folder is dropped, so the structure the
    77	    // customer sent is preserved rather than flattened — `brand/` and `fonts/` mean
    78	    // something to ingest.
    79	    const relative = String(form.get(`path:${file.name}`) ?? file.name)
    80	    if (relative.includes('..') || relative.startsWith('/')) {
    81	      return Response.json({ error: `refusing a path, not a filename: ${relative}` }, { status: 400 })
    82	    }
    83	    if (!/\.(md|json|svg|png|jpg|jpeg|ttf|otf|woff2?)$/i.test(relative)) continue
    84	    if (file.size > 8 * 1024 * 1024) {
    85	      return Response.json({ error: `${relative} is larger than 8 MB` }, { status: 400 })
    86	    }
    87	    const target = join(staging, relative)
    88	    mkdirSync(join(target, '..'), { recursive: true })
    89	    writeFileSync(target, new Uint8Array(await file.arrayBuffer()))
    90	    stored.push(relative)
    91	  }
    92	  if (stored.length === 0) {
    93	    return Response.json({ error: 'none of those files are brand files we accept' }, { status: 400 })
    94	  }
    95	
    96	  // The kit row first, as `pending`. A launcher refuses to run against a kit that is
    97	  // not `ready`, so a half-ingested brand cannot produce an ad missing its fonts.
    98	  await serviceFetch('/rest/v1/brand_kits', {
    99	    method: 'POST',
    100	    body: JSON.stringify({
    101	      id: kitId,
    102	      customer_id: customerId,
    103	      display_name: displayName,
    104	      ingest_status: 'pending',
    105	    }),
    106	  })
    107	
    108	  const child = spawn('npx', ['tsx', 'scripts/ingest-to-supabase.ts', '--dir', staging, '--kit', kitId], {
    109	    cwd: join(process.cwd(), '..', 'eval'),
    110	    detached: true,
    111	    stdio: 'ignore',
    112	  })
    113	  child.unref()
    114	
    115	  return Response.json({
    116	    ok: true,
    117	    customer_id: customerId,
    118	    kit_id: kitId,
    119	    files: stored.length,
    120	    ingesting: true,
    121	  })
    122	}

    RESULT: 1	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
    2	import { env, serviceFetch, verifyUserToken } from '@/lib/server'

    4	/**
    5	 * Upload files into a brand kit.
    6	 *
    7	 * Forwarded with the *session* token, never `service_role`, so the storage policy is
    8	 * what decides: a write is allowed only under a kit id belonging to this customer.
    9	 * That means the tenancy check is not code in this handler that could be got wrong —
    10	 * it is the same rule that governs every other read and write in the system.
    11	 *
    12	 * Path traversal is refused rather than sanitised. A filename is a filename; anything
    13	 * containing a separator or `..` is not one, and quietly rewriting it would hide a
    14	 * caller doing something odd.
    15	 */
    16	const ALLOWED = /\.(md|json|svg|png|jpg|jpeg|ttf|woff2)$/i
    17	const MAX_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024
    18	
    19	export async function POST(request: Request) {
    20	  const store = await cookies()
    21	  const token = store.get('cq_session')?.value
    22	  if (!token || !verifyUserToken(token)) {
    23	    return Response.json({ error: 'not signed in' }, { status: 401 })
    24	  }
    25	
    26	  const form = await request.formData()
    27	  const kitId = String(form.get('kit_id') ?? '')
    28	  if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$/.test(kitId)) {
    29	    return Response.json({ error: 'kit_id is not a valid id' }, { status: 400 })
    30	  }
    31	
    32	  const files = form.getAll('files').filter((f): f is File => f instanceof File)
    33	  if (files.length === 0) return Response.json({ error: 'no files' }, { status: 400 })
    34	
    35	  /**
    36	   * Uploading an inspiration rather than a brand file.
    37	   *
    38	   * An inspiration has to be named for the brand that owns it. The bucket prefix already
    39	   * isolates it, so the naming rule is not what keeps customers apart — it is what keeps a
    40	   * file's name and its location honest, so "belongs to" is checkable by looking rather
    41	   * than by trusting where someone put it.
    42	   *
    43	   * Slugs are derived from the kit's own row, so a new brand needs no code change.
    44	   */
    45	  const asInspiration = String(form.get('target') ?? '') === 'inspirations'
    46	  let brandSlugs: string[] = []
    47	  if (asInspiration) {
    48	    const rows = await serviceFetch(
    49	      `/rest/v1/brand_kits?id=eq.${encodeURIComponent(kitId)}&select=id,customer_id,display_name`,
    50	    )
    51	    const kit = Array.isArray(rows) ? rows[0] : null
    52	    if (!kit) return Response.json({ error: `no kit ${kitId}` }, { status: 404 })
    53	    const clean = (value: string) =>
    54	      String(value).toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-').replace(/^-|-$/g, '')
    55	    brandSlugs = [
    56	      ...new Set([
    57	        clean(kit.customer_id),
    58	        clean(kit.display_name),
    59	        clean(kitId).replace(/^bk-/, '').replace(/-\d{4}$/, ''),
    60	      ].filter(Boolean)),
    61	    ]
    62	  }
    63	
    64	  const { SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY } = env()
    65	  const stored: string[] = []
    66	
    67	  for (const file of files) {
    68	    const name = file.name
    69	    if (name.includes('/') || name.includes('\\') || name.includes('..')) {
    70	      return Response.json({ error: `refusing a path, not a filename: ${name}` }, { status: 400 })
    71	    }
    72	    if (!ALLOWED.test(name)) {
    73	      return Response.json({ error: `${name} is not a brand file type we accept` }, { status: 400 })
    74	    }
    75	    if (file.size > MAX_BYTES) {
    76	      return Response.json({ error: `${name} is larger than 8 MB` }, { status: 400 })
    77	    }
    78	
    79	    if (asInspiration) {
    80	      if (!/\.(png|jpe?g|webp)$/i.test(name)) {
    81	        return Response.json({ error: `an inspiration must be an image: ${name}` }, { status: 400 })
    82	      }
    83	      const lower = name.toLowerCase()
    84	      if (!brandSlugs.some((slug) => lower.startsWith(`${slug}-`) || lower.startsWith(`${slug}_`))) {
    85	        return Response.json(
    86	          {
    87	            error:
    88	              `"${name}" must start with this brand's name. Try ` +
    89	              `${brandSlugs[0]}-${name.replace(/^[^a-z0-9]*/i, '')}`,
    90	            expected: brandSlugs,
    91	          },
    92	          { status: 400 },
    93	        )
    94	      }
    95	    }
    96	
    97	    // Documents at the kit root, everything else where ingest expects to find it, so an
    98	    // upload lands where the next ingest will look.
    99	    const folder = asInspiration
    100	      ? 'inspirations'
    101	      : /\.(ttf|woff2)$/i.test(name)
    102	        ? 'fonts'
    103	        : /\.(md)$/i.test(name)
    104	          ? ''
    105	          : 'brand'
    106	    const key = folder ? `${kitId}/${folder}/${name}` : `${kitId}/${name}`
    107	
    108	    const response = await fetch(`${SUPABASE_URL}/storage/v1/object/brains/${key}`, {
    109	      method: 'POST',
    110	      headers: {
    111	        apikey: SUPABASE_ANON_KEY,
    112	        Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
    113	        'Content-Type': file.type || 'application/octet-stream',
    114	        'x-upsert': 'true',
    115	      },
    116	      body: new Uint8Array(await file.arrayBuffer()),
    117	    })
    118	    if (!response.ok) {
    119	      const body = await response.text()
    120	      return Response.json(
    121	        { error: `could not store ${name}: ${response.status} ${body.slice(0, 160)}`, stored },
    122	        { status: 400 },
    123	      )
    124	    }
    125	    stored.push(key)
    126	  }
    127	
    128	  return Response.json({ ok: true, stored })
    129	}

    import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
    import { session } from '@/lib/read'
    import { serviceFetch } from '@/lib/server'
    import CustomersClient from './customers-client'
    
    /**
     * Add a customer, and see what ingest made of every kit.
     *
     * Listing all customers uses the privileged key on purpose: this is an operator screen
     * in a local deployment, and its whole job is to show kits that do not belong to the
     * signed-in customer yet. Nothing here can read a kit's *work* — only its ingest
     * outcome, which is the same information the person who uploaded it needs.
     */
    export default async function CustomersPage() {
      const current = await session()
      if (!current) redirect('/')
    
      const kits = (await serviceFetch(
        '/rest/v1/brand_kits?select=id,customer_id,display_name,ingest_status&order=customer_id',
      )) as { id: string; customer_id: string; display_name: string; ingest_status: string }[]
    
      const findings = (await serviceFetch(
        '/rest/v1/findings?revision_id=is.null&select=kit_id,code,severity,detail',
      )) as { kit_id: string | null; code: string; severity: string; detail: string }[]
    
      const assets = (await serviceFetch(
        '/rest/v1/brand_assets?select=kit_id,available',
      )) as { kit_id: string; available: boolean }[]
    
      const fonts = (await serviceFetch('/rest/v1/brand_fonts?select=kit_id')) as { kit_id: string }[]
    
      return (
        <CustomersClient
          currentCustomer={current.customerId}
          kits={kits.map((k) => ({
            ...k,
            usable: assets.filter((a) => a.kit_id === k.id && a.available).length,
            fonts: fonts.filter((f) => f.kit_id === k.id).length,
            findings: findings.filter((f) => f.kit_id === k.id).length,
            blockers: findings.filter((f) => f.kit_id === k.id && f.severity === 'blocker'),
          }))}
        />
      )
    }

    export default async function Home() {

        '/rest/v1/brand_kits?select=id,customer_id,display_name,ingest_status&order=customer_id',
      )) as { id: string; customer_id: string; display_name: string; ingest_status: string }[]

        list.push(kit)

      )

Before I move it — there's a blocker worth knowing about.

The switch-customer page is [app/page.tsx](web/app/page.tsx) → [sign-in.tsx](web/app/sign-in.tsx), and by definition you have **no session** there. But `/customers` redirects to `/` without one ([customers/page.tsx:19](web/app/customers/page.tsx#L19)), and `/api/customer` returns 401 without one ([api/customer/route.ts:28](web/app/api/customer/route.ts#L28)) — deliberately, with the comment *"this is an operator action in a single-tenant local deployment, not a public sign-up."*

So a button there would bounce straight back to the sign-in screen. Making it work means letting a customer be created **before** anyone signs in, which is a change to that guard rather than a button.

## The guard change, stated plainly

`/customers` and `POST /api/customer` no longer require a session — that was necessary, since the switch-customer screen has none by definition. Verified: `/customers` now returns **200** with no cookie instead of redirecting.

What still protects it, and what doesn't:

- **Still holds** — a new customer id or kit id that already exists is refused ([route.ts:46-58](web/app/api/customer/route.ts#L46-L58)). This cannot adopt or write into a brand someone already owns. Every other route still reads and writes with the session token under the database's own policies, so existing customers' data is untouched by this.
- **The removed check was never a tenancy boundary** — it accepted *any* session, including another customer's. It gated discovery, not ownership.
- **No longer holds** — creating a *new* tenant is open. Correct for a passwordless local trial; it's the first thing to put behind real auth if this were deployed. I wrote that tradeoff into the route as a comment rather than leaving it implicit.

    RESULT: # Northwind Foods
    
    A cold-chain logistics company for fresh produce. Sells to grocery buyers and
    distribution managers. Sober, precise, never playful about food safety.
    
    ## Palette
    
    - primary: #14532D
    - secondary: #4D7C0F
    - accent: #F59E0B
    - surface: #FFFFFF
    - ink: #14181A
    - muted: #6B7280
    
    ## Type
    
    - heading: Barlow
    - body: Barlow
    
    ## Type scale
    
    - h1: 46px
    - h2: 34px
    - h3: 22px
    - body: 17px
    - caption: 13px
    
    ## Shape
    
    - border-radius: 6px
    - Cards and image containers use the 6px corner. Buttons use the same.
    
    ## Applying it
    
    Headline type is Barlow 700, set tight. An h1 is 46px on every canvas. If the
    headline does not fit at 46, cut the copy; do not scale the type. Body copy is
    Barlow 400, and the eyebrow above a headline is Barlow 600 at caption size,
    letterspaced, in the accent.
    
    The accent carries the call to action and almost nothing else. A primary button
    is a solid fill of #F59E0B with ink label text at Barlow 600. Secondary buttons
    are a 1px #F59E0B outline on surface with the label in the same amber. Never
    tint the accent, and never use it as a background for a region larger than a
    button.
    
    Photography is refrigerated warehouses, pallets and produce in cold light.
    Never a person holding food. Never a plated meal.

One deliberate difference from emplifi: emplifi comes out with four extra `review` findings (its `partner-lockup.svg` is tagged `bk-kahua-2026`, and its `tokens.json` disagrees with DESIGN.md in three places). Those are the planted bugs. I built Harborline **without** them, so it's a clean control — if a run against it misbehaves, the kit isn't the reason.

## To test it

On the sign-in screen (or Review), hit **+ Add customer**, then type the name exactly:

```
Harborline
```

That slugs to `harborline` and derives `bk-harborline-2026`, which is what the manifest declares — so no mismatch. Then drop the `harborline` folder itself (not its contents; the client strips the top folder's name so `brand/` and `fonts/` survive).

Expect `pending` → refresh → `ready`, 3 assets, 4 fonts, 3 findings none blocking.

Two notes:
- The Barlow files are copies from kahua's kit — Barlow is SIL OFL, so redistributing it in a second kit is fine, and reusing a proven font file means a font problem in your test is a pipeline problem, not a file problem. Kahua's originals are untouched.
- Font `.ttf` isn't in `/api/kit`'s allow-list, but that route isn't involved here — `/api/customer` accepts `ttf|otf|woff2?` and ingest uploads them, which the dry run confirms as 11 objects including all four fonts.

## Disqualifiers — all seven clear

| # | Disqualifier | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Anything but the agent moves work out of the box | **Clear.** Only `sandbox.files.write` appears in the launchers ([launch-deploy.ts:416](eval/scripts/launch-deploy.ts#L416), [launch-run.ts:600](eval/scripts/launch-run.ts#L600)) — writes *in*, never reads out. `results/*/outputs/*.png` came from `/storage/v1/object/work/...` ([interleave-test.sh:190](eval/scripts/interleave-test.sh#L190)), i.e. Supabase, not the box. |
| 2 | A Kahua box and an Emplifi box | **Clear.** `cq-generation` / `cq-deployment`. No tenant in any box identity; asserted at [build.ts:185](sandbox/build.ts#L185). Two images is explicitly permitted — *"one image or two is your call."* |
| 3 | Backend launching the agent as a subprocess on its own box | **Clear.** The agent process only ever runs via `sandbox.commands.run` inside E2B. What spawns locally is the *launcher* and *ingest* — neither is an agent. |
| 4 | Any agent run on your laptop | **Clear.** No local agent path. |
| 5 | Work that exists only on a box | **The open one.** See below. |
| 6 | A hardcoded ordering | **Clear.** Interleave ran 5 steps, 2 tenants, concurrent boxes, 10 renders. |
| 7 | `.env` committed | **Clear.** Gitignored, `git ls-files` count 0. |

## Verification actually run

- `npm test` — **292 passed**, 14 files
- The two isolation suites were *skipping* — they self-report loudly, which is right, but it means nothing was proving isolation. They skip on a local TLS-interception error, not a code fault. Ran them properly: **29/29 passed** against the real database and real storage, including *"cannot read another revision's object"* and *"sees its own asset even when filed under the other customer."*

**Worth knowing:** `npm test` alone silently leaves your strongest evidence unrun. To get it you need `set -a && . ../.env && set +a && NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 npx vitest run tests/tenant-isolation.test.ts tests/storage-rls.test.ts`.

## Three deploy bugs I diagnosed are now fixed in the tree

Not by me this turn — they landed between my read and now, and they're correct:

- Recording scoped by `run_id` with `order=created_at.desc` ([launch-deploy.ts:443](eval/scripts/launch-deploy.ts#L443))
- `resolveDeployStatus` makes the agent's verdict a **ceiling** ([deploy-fields.ts:69](eval/src/deploy-fields.ts#L69)) — `published` only survives with recording *and* url; 14 tests cover it
- `primaryTextFrom(copy)` derives Primary text and it's a required field ([launch-deploy.ts:197](eval/scripts/launch-deploy.ts#L197)), so `COPY_MAPPING_MISSING` can't recur

Bonus: `sandbox.kill()` moved into a nested `finally`, so a database failure can no longer leak a running box.

# Sandbox death: four options

First, the correction your idea needs. **You cannot write a transcript "before a kill."** An external kill gives the box no warning — no signal, no shutdown hook, nothing runs after it. So a transcript written at the end is exactly the transcript you lose. It has to be **streamed as it happens**, or it isn't there when you need it.

Second: don't append transcripts *into* hydration. Attempt 3 would carry attempts 1 and 2 in full, hydration is saved for audit forever, and it grows without bound. Hydrate a **compacted resume block** instead.

### Option A — Stream the transcript as an artifact *(do this one)*

Every tool call and result appends one line to `work/transcript-<run>.jsonl`, flushed to storage every ~30s and on every `save_work`. Uses the append-only save path that already exists.

- Satisfies the brief's transcript ask directly
- Survives an unannounced kill — you lose at most 30 seconds
- Costs one small upload per 30s
- Recovers: the reasoning, so you can see *where* it died

### Option B — `already_saved` in hydration *(do this one too)*

On retry the launcher reads the artifacts already durable for that revision and hydrates the list with paths and digests, plus one instruction: *these exist; do not remake them.*

- Directly answers the brief's billing scenario — *"the image model call already succeeded and you've been billed for it"* — a plate on disk is never regenerated
- Needs plates saved the moment they're generated, before overlay. Worth checking; `save_work` is a command the agent calls, so the skill decides when
- This is the one that makes retry *cheap* rather than merely *possible*

### Option C — `runs.last_heartbeat_at` + a reaper

Box writes a heartbeat every 30s; anything with three missed beats is marked `failed`, `exit_reason: 'no heartbeat'`.

- Fixes phantom rows for real, at the source, instead of in the UI's `sandbox_id` check
- Turns "died" from something a human notices into a state the system knows
- Doesn't recover anything by itself — it's what makes A and B *trigger*

### Option D — `prior_decisions` block

A compacted list of choices the dead attempt made (which reverse logo, which ground, which inspiration) so attempt 2 doesn't re-litigate them and produce a visibly different ad.

- Cheapest of the four
- Optional — a nice-to-have next to A/B/C

**My recommendation: C then A then B**, in that order. C is the smallest and unblocks knowing a run died at all; A gives you the debugging surface the brief asks for; B is what makes retry not cost money twice. Then crash a box on purpose and write the resulting table — which states a retry recovers, which need you in the database — straight into DECISIONS.md. That's the deliverable, and the crash is how you find out rather than guess.

Say which you want and I'll propose the concrete edits before touching anything.

## What was wrong

Your upload was fine. The files were already sitting correctly in storage. What broke was **where ingest looked for them.**

A browser reports each file's path relative to the folder that was *chosen*, so the staged kit landed as:

```
.staging-kits/bk-harborline-2026/harborline/DESIGN.md
                                 ^^^^^^^^^^ a wrapper level ingest didn't expect
```

Ingest checked the root, found no `DESIGN.md`, and marked a complete brand `blocked` — one finding, no explanation, files already stored. Exactly the thing you described: saved, and reported as not ingested.

## Two changes

**1. Ingest finds the brain instead of assuming it** — [ingest-to-supabase.ts:217](eval/scripts/ingest-to-supabase.ts#L217)

`resolveBrainRoot()` descends one wrapper level when the directory handed over doesn't look like a brain but exactly one child does, and prints which level it used. Cause-agnostic — it doesn't matter which folder someone picks.

It deliberately does **not** guess when two children look like brains. That means the upload holds more than one brand, and silently picking one is how the wrong brand gets ingested under this kit's id. That case still blocks, which is correct.

**2. Ingest's output is kept** — [api/customer/route.ts:108](web/app/api/customer/route.ts#L108)

It ran `stdio: 'ignore'`, so the reason for the failure was in output nobody kept — a detached job whose only trace was a status column. Now it appends to `web/.launch-logs/ingest-<kitId>.log`.

    20	export function currentDigest(): string {
    21	  const files: Record<string, string> = {}
    22	  const add = (label: string, path: string) => {
    23	    files[label] = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(path)).digest('hex').slice(0, 16)
    24	  }
    25	  add('agent.generate.ts', join(ROOT, 'agent.generate.ts'))
    26	  add('agent.deploy.ts', join(ROOT, 'agent.deploy.ts'))
    27	  add('save_work.mjs', join(ROOT, 'save_work.mjs'))
    28	  add('template.generation.ts', join(ROOT, 'template.generation.ts'))
    29	  add('template.deployment.ts', join(ROOT, 'template.deployment.ts'))
    30	  for (const name of BAKED_SKILLS) add(`skill:${name}`, join(REPO, '.claude', 'skills', name, 'SKILL.md'))
    31	  for (const file of BAKED_TOOLKIT) add(`toolkit:${file}`, join(REPO, 'eval', 'src', file))
    32	  const combined = Object.keys(files).sort().map((k) => `${k}:${files[k]}`).join('\n')
    33	  return createHash('sha256').update(combined).digest('hex')
    34	}
    35	
    36	export interface StampCheck {
    37	  fresh: boolean
    38	  reason: string
    39	  changed: string[]
    40	}
    41	
    42	export function checkStamp(): StampCheck {
    43	  const stampPath = join(ROOT, '.build-stamp.json')
    44	  if (!existsSync(stampPath)) {
    45	    return { fresh: false, reason: 'no .build-stamp.json — the templates have never been built from this tree', changed: [] }
    46	  }
    47	  const stamp = JSON.parse(readFileSync(stampPath, 'utf8')) as {
    48	    digest: string
    49	    built: string[]
    50	    at: string
    51	    files: Record<string, string>
    52	  }
    53	  if (stamp.digest === currentDigest()) {
    54	    return { fresh: true, reason: `templates match source (built ${stamp.at})`, changed: [] }
    55	  }
    56	
    57	  // Name the files that moved. "Something changed" sends someone hunting; a list
    58	  // tells them immediately whether it matters.
    59	  const changed: string[] = []
    60	  const add = (label: string, path: string) => {
    61	    const now = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(path)).digest('hex').slice(0, 16)
    62	    if (stamp.files[label] !== now) changed.push(label)
    63	  }
    64	  add('agent.generate.ts', join(ROOT, 'agent.generate.ts'))
    65	  add('agent.deploy.ts', join(ROOT, 'agent.deploy.ts'))
    66	  add('save_work.mjs', join(ROOT, 'save_work.mjs'))
    67	  add('template.generation.ts', join(ROOT, 'template.generation.ts'))
    68	  add('template.deployment.ts', join(ROOT, 'template.deployment.ts'))
    69	  for (const name of BAKED_SKILLS) add(`skill:${name}`, join(REPO, '.claude', 'skills', name, 'SKILL.md'))
    70	  for (const file of BAKED_TOOLKIT) add(`toolkit:${file}`, join(REPO, 'eval', 'src', file))
    71	
    72	  return {
    73	    fresh: false,
    74	    reason: `${changed.length} baked file(s) changed since the last build (${stamp.at})`,
    75	    changed,
    76	  }
    77	}
    78	
    79	if (process.argv[1]?.endsWith('check-stamp.ts')) {
    80	  const result = checkStamp()
    81	  console.log(result.fresh ? `FRESH — ${result.reason}` : `STALE — ${result.reason}`)
    82	  for (const c of result.changed) console.log(`  changed: ${c}`)
    83	  if (!result.fresh) console.log('\n  run: npm run build --prefix sandbox\n')
    84	  process.exit(result.fresh ? 0 : 1)
    85	}

## What was actually wrong

The guard was right that something was stale, but wrong to stop *you*. `agent.deploy.ts` and `skill:deploy-campaign` are baked into the **deployment** image only — neither is in the generation image — yet one flat digest covered both templates, so a deploy-side edit refused a generation launch. A guard that blocks correct work is one you learn to `--allow-stale` past, and then it isn't a guard.

## Freshness is now per template

- **[check-stamp.ts](sandbox/check-stamp.ts)** — a `BAKED` map declaring what each image contains, read off the `.copy()` calls in each template. `checkStamp('generation')` digests only generation's files. `save_work.mjs` is in both lists because both bake it; the toolkit is generation-only, since the deployment template copies no toolkit.
- **[build.ts](sandbox/build.ts)** — `writeStamp` now imports those lists instead of keeping a second copy, and writes one digest per template. The duplicate list was the real hazard: add a file to one copy and an image bakes something the stamp never watches, so editing it never triggers a rebuild.
- **[launch-run.ts:48](eval/scripts/launch-run.ts#L48)** → `checkStamp('generation')`, **[launch-deploy.ts:30](eval/scripts/launch-deploy.ts#L30)** → `checkStamp('deployment')`.
- A stamp written before this split reports **stale**, not fresh — the honest answer to "was this image built from a list I can't see" is no.

--- ASSISTANT [2026-08-11 15:07:26] ---
Short answer: **no — a transcript can't be saved via the hydration file.** The directions are opposite. But your instinct is half right, and I need to correct the other half first because it matters for the walkthrough.

## The hydration file isn't stored

I checked. Nothing persists it:

- `launch-run.ts` writes it into the box with `sandbox.files.write`, and that's the only copy
- `--dump-hydration` writes a local copy, but it's opt-in and off by default — a debugging aid, not durable state
- **nothing ever reads a prior hydration back** — the only readers are the two agents, reading the file in their own box

So if you say "we store the hydration file so a killed sandbox can resume," that's not what the code does, and it's the kind of claim he'll pull on.

## What actually makes you safe is better than that

Hydration is **rebuilt from Supabase on every launch.** Your run an hour ago proves it:

```
brand: pulled 10 file(s) from brains/bk-harborline1-2026/
hydration: 12 mounts, 10 kit files, no gaps, no leaks
```

Nothing was replayed from a previous box. The database and the bucket are the state; hydration is *derived* from them. That's the stronger answer to *"work that exists only on a box"* — and it's stronger precisely **because** it isn't stored. A stored hydration would carry expired signed URLs and a snapshot of a brand that may have changed. A derived one can't go stale.

That's the sentence for DECISIONS.md: *state lives in Postgres and storage; hydration is a derived artifact, regenerated per attempt, never replayed.*

## Now your question — the two directions

```
hydration.json      launcher ──► box      INPUT   written by us, read by the agent
transcript          box ──► storage       OUTPUT  written by the agent, via save_work
```

A transcript is output. It cannot ride the input channel, and it must not be collected by us — *"Anything other than the agent moves work out of the box"* is a disqualifier. So it leaves the box the same way a render does: the agent writes it into the work tree, `save_work` uploads the bytes and inserts the artifact row.

**Where the hydration file does come in is the return trip.** On attempt 2, the launcher reads the prior attempt's transcript *out of storage* and includes it in the new hydration. So:

```
attempt 1:  box ──save_work──► storage        (transcript persisted)
attempt 2:  storage ──launcher──► hydration ──► box   (agent sees what attempt 1 did)
```

Your instinct was right about hydration carrying it — just on the way **in**, not out.

## What that costs

One line, essentially. `roleOf` in `save_work.mjs` currently sends `transcript/…` to `other`, and `other` is refused for the deploy role by [0016](supabase/migrations/0016_deploy_fields_and_result.sql#L33) — so it needs to classify as `result`. Note `roleOf` already does this loosely for `RESULT*.json`, and the comment there records it being tightened-then-loosened twice for exactly this reason.

Everything else is the agent writing a file, which it already knows how to do.

The open question is still whether you need it at all — the crash test answers that. Want me to run the kill test now, or do the `roleOf` line first?

## One hazard I found while implementing, and closed

`save_work` sets the revision to `partial` before saving. A flush every 30 seconds would therefore keep re-marking it — and on a **deploy** box the revision it relabels is an *approved* one. A transcript flush would have quietly demoted approved work, and if the box died it would stay demoted.

`--only` now skips the status write entirely. A targeted flush saves bytes and makes no claim about the run's progress. This wasn't in the plan; I'd rather tell you than let you find it.

## Why this shouldn't break a deploy

- `Transcript.line()` swallows its own errors — it can't take down a run it's only describing
- `flush()` catches too, and logs to stderr rather than throwing
- `--only transcript` means a flush cannot save a render, a plate, an html file or a recording
- `--only` also skips the `partial` revision write, so a flush can't demote your approved revision
- The `--final` save at the end is unchanged

**The one real risk:** `transcript.ts` must be present in the image, because a missing module is a box that won't start at all, not a degraded transcript. That's what the `.copy()` line and this rebuild are for — and it's why the next deploy run is the real test.

When the build lands I'll confirm both images read FRESH. Then run one deploy and check three things: transcript segments arrive as `result` artifacts, the recording still saves, and `RESULT-<run>.json` still saves. If any of those regress, it's a one-file revert plus a rebuild.

# How the filesystem was made and structured

The brief's one idea is *everything is a file system — files and skills hydrated in different orders at different times*. Here's how that's literally true in this system.

## Three tiers, decided by lifetime

The brief names them: what's the same every run, what's the same for one customer, what lives for one job. Each gets a different *mechanism*, and the mechanism is chosen by how often the thing changes.

| Tier | Lives in | Gets in by | Changes when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Same every run | the E2B image | baked at build time | you rebuild |
| Same per customer | `brains` bucket | pulled fresh, every run | the brand changes |
| One job only | Postgres → `hydration.json` | written into the box at launch | every run |

**Baked** — the skill, the toolkit, `save_work`. These are the contract and the tooling, identical for every tenant, so they belong to the image. Verified by digest at launch, per template, which is the freshness guard you hit twice today.

**Pulled** — the brain. Never baked, and this is the load-bearing decision: *"the moment a box already knows which brand it serves, you've lost."* Every launch lists `brains/<kitId>/` and downloads it. Your Harborline run: `brand: pulled 10 file(s) from brains/bk-harborline1-2026/`. A rebrand needs no rebuild because the image never contained a brand.

**Written** — `hydration.json`, plus inspirations and the parent revision's files. Derived from Postgres at launch, never replayed.

## Two buckets, and the prefix is the boundary

```
brains/<kitId>/DESIGN.md              the brand — outranks every other artifact
              /README.md
              /brand/asset_manifest.json
              /brand/*.svg
              /fonts/<family>_<weight>_<style>.ttf
              /inspirations/<brand>-*.png

work/<request-id>/rev-<n>/renders/<canvas>.png
                         /html_<canvas>/index.html
                         /html_<canvas>/assets/plate.png
                         /deploy/page@<hash>.webm
                         /deploy/RESULT-<run>.json
                         /transcript/<run>-000.jsonl
                         /RESULT.json
```

The **first path segment is the security boundary.** Storage policy scopes reads by it, so a kit's files are readable only under its own id. That's why ingest keys uploads by the *owning* kit from the manifest rather than the folder a file was found in — and why an uploaded manifest can't assign ownership. Row-level and object-level isolation have to agree, and only the owning id makes them agree.

`work/` is prefixed by request and revision, which is what makes save-out append-only: `unique (revision_id, relative_path)`. A path already stored comes back 409 and is skipped. **A box cannot rewrite its own history** — that's the property the transcript had to be designed around today, which is why segments and not one growing file.

## Inside the box

```
/home/user/hydration.json                     what to make — the only job-specific input
          /brain/DESIGN.md, brand/…, fonts/…  this customer's brand, pulled this run
          /inspirations/…                     chosen, prefix-checked against the brand
          /parent/…                           the revision being edited, for an edit
          /.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md      the contract, baked
          /toolkit/…                          deterministic tooling, baked
          /work/                              CQ_WORK_DIR — everything the run produces
          /usr/local/bin/save_work            the only way out
```

The shape is deliberate: **inputs are scattered by tier, outputs are one tree.** `save_work` walks `/home/user/work` and mirrors it to `work/<request>/rev-<n>/`, deciding each file's role from its path — `renders/` → render, `html_*/assets/plate.png` → plate, `transcript/` → result. *One tree in, one tree out*, so nothing has to reconcile a flat key space against a nested one.

## Direction is the invariant

```
in :  image (baked) + bucket (pulled) + Postgres (derived) ──► box
out:  box ──save_work──► bucket + artifact rows
```

Nothing outside the box reaches in to collect anything — `sandbox.files.write` appears in the launchers, and no read ever does. That's the first disqualifier, and it's why your question earlier about saving the transcript through hydration had to be answered "no": hydration is the input channel. The transcript leaves the way a render leaves, and returns through the *next* attempt's hydration.

## What this buys

- **A rebrand can't need a rebuild** — the brand was never in the image
- **A killed box loses nothing that was saved** — state is in Postgres and the bucket; hydration is derived, so a retry rebuilds it rather than resurrecting anything
- **No box knows its tenant** — identity is the provider's handle, and the templates are named for the task class, which the brief explicitly permits
- **Ordering can't matter** — every run reads its own inputs fresh, which is why the interleave passed with two tenants in concurrent boxes

Want this as a section in DECISIONS.md? It would slot in beside §The model, in one page — though check whether that section already says most of it before I duplicate anything.
